title: Core sheet
summary: What you memorise, what you recognise, what you look up.

sections.title: Overview
sections.markdown:
*16 November 2026, updated after the third review. Swedish YKI intermediate test, target level 3. This sheet is the whole core, in three layers; the rest of the plan is a library.*

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]** This applies to every Swedish line on this sheet.

sections.title: The three layers, and what they mean for your time
sections.markdown:
| Layer | What it means | What it costs you | Sections |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ACTIVE CORE** | Recall it and use it without notes, in speaking and in writing. | This is where your memorising time goes: the daily cards (at most 8 new a day), cover-and-say, the swap drill and the transfer test. | 1–9 |
| **RECOGNITION CORE** | Understand it when you hear it or read it. You do not have to say or write it. | No production drill. Hear it, match it to the English, and notice it on task cards and in recordings, inside the day's review and listening blocks. | 10–11 |
| **REFERENCE** | Look it up when a task needs it. | No compulsory memorising. Lines you use often will stick by themselves. | 12–13 |

Sections 14–15 are study rules, not language to learn.

**The counts overlap.** The groups share lines. *Jag tycker att …* is an opinion frame and the opinion opening; *Till exempel …* is a frame and rescue phrase 7; *Tyvärr kan jag inte …* is a frame and reaction 10; *Det var allt jag ville säga.* is a closing and rescue phrase 8. The numbers in brackets say how big each group is. They are not a count of unique sentences, so do not add them up.

sections.title: How to use this sheet
sections.markdown:
- **Learn frames, not whole answers.** A frame is a sentence with a gap [ ] that you fill with the card's details. The example answers show a shape; never learn one as a whole answer.
- **Audio:** hear every line before you say it: from your teacher, a Swedish voice, or the book's QR tracks. For Days 1–14 the single list of lines to hear is `YKI-AUDIO-LIST-DAYS-1-14.md`.
- **On a task card:** underline what it asks for, pick one main answer shape (the "engine", section 2) and borrow single moves from other engines when the card asks for them, open and close the way the situation needs (section 4), and fill the shape.
- **When to stop.** In a call or a message, stop when every point is covered. In an opinion or a story task, a ticked checklist is the minimum, not the finish: develop each point with a reason, an example and a link word (section 2, engine 4).
- **Answer length (practice aims, not exam rules).** Practise at about 80 words a minute: 20 seconds holds about 25–33 words, 25 seconds about 33–40, 1 minute about 80 and 1.5 minutes about 120.
- **Move on by Green, Amber or Red** (section 14), not by counts.
- **With an AI chat:** paste this sheet in and ask it to quiz you from the English. It is not an official rater, and its Swedish can be wrong.

---

sections.title: 1. Five grammar rules these frames use
sections.markdown:
1. **The finite verb comes second.** The finite verb is the verb that shows the time (*är, bor, kan, jobbade*). In a main clause it is the second unit, and a unit can be several words (*I dag*, *Förra veckan*, *På fredag klockan tio*). If a time, a place or a word like *tyvärr* (unfortunately) comes first, the subject moves after the verb: *I dag jobbar jag hemma.* (Today I'm working at home.) Not *I dag jag jobbar*.
2. **Questions.** A yes/no question starts with the finite verb: *Har du tid i morgon?* (Do you have time tomorrow?) An ordinary question starts with the question word, then the verb: *Var bor du?* (Where do you live?) When the question word is the subject, the verb follows at once: *Vem kommer?* (Who is coming?) Inside a longer sentence (an indirect question), use subject–verb order: *Jag undrar när kursen börjar.* (I wonder when the course starts.) If the question word is the subject there, add *som*: *Vet du vem som kommer?* (Do you know who is coming?)
3. ***inte* (not)** comes after the finite verb in a main clause: *Jag kan inte komma.* (I can't come.) In a basic subordinate clause (after *att, eftersom, om* and *när*), the subject comes first, then *inte*, then the finite verb: *Problemet är att den inte startar.* (The problem is that it doesn't start.) / *… eftersom jag inte har tid.* (… because I don't have time.) *redan* (already) and *alltid* (always) move the same way.
4. **One verb form for every person:** *jag bor, du bor, vi bor.* Don't use *är* before another verb to make the present tense: *Jag bor i Esbo*, not *Jag är bor i Esbo*. After *kan, vill, måste, ska, skulle* and *brukar* comes the base form, with no *att*: *Jag vill boka en tid.* (I want to book an appointment.)
5. ***den, det, de* (it, it, they).** *den* for an *en*-word (*en cykel*: *Den är tre år gammal.*). *det* for an *ett*-word, and the adjective usually adds *-t* (*ett skrivbord*: *Det är två år gammalt.*); that is a common pattern, not a law (*bra* never changes, and *liten* becomes *litet*). *de* for a plural, with *-a* (*De är tre år gamla.*).

sections.title: 2. The six answer shapes ("engines")
sections.markdown:
Pick one **main** engine per task: it tells you what to say, in what order. Then borrow single moves from the other engines when the card asks for them. A complaint about a repair, for example, runs on Fix, borrows the Story sequence to say what happened (*Först … Sedan … Till slut …*) and an Ask line for the new time (*Har ni en ledig tid på torsdag?*). The situation, not the engine, decides how you open and close (section 4).

### Engine 1: Ask (request, booking, information)

**Shape:** who I am → what I want → one or two questions → confirm → thanks.

**Example, a call to book an appointment (Day 4's lines; the parts in "…" are the other voice):**
*Hej, det här är Alex Kumar. Jag skulle vilja boka en tid.* … *Jag kan inte komma på morgonen. Kan jag komma efter klockan fyra?* … *Tack för hjälpen! Hej då!*
(Hi, this is Alex Kumar. I would like to book an appointment. … I can't come in the morning. Can I come after four? … Thanks for the help! Bye!)

The price question (*Hur mycket kostar besöket?*, How much does the visit cost?) and the confirm line (*Okej, då säger vi …*) join the call on Day 12.

### Engine 2: Fix (complaint, repair, asking someone to stop)

**Shape:** what is wrong → since when → why it matters → what I want → close.

**Example, a call to a repair firm (an official sample type):**
*Hej, det här är Alex Kumar. Jag ringer angående min tvättmaskin. Den är fortfarande trasig. En reparatör var här i tisdags, men den fungerar fortfarande inte. Vi är fyra personer och vi behöver tvättmaskinen varje dag. Kan ni komma i morgon eller på torsdag?*
(Hi, this is Alex Kumar. I'm calling about my washing machine. It is still broken. A repair person was here last Tuesday, but it still doesn't work. We are four people and we need the washing machine every day. Can you come tomorrow or on Thursday?)

### Engine 3: Social (react, thank, apologise, invite, refuse)

**Shape:** react or say the news → one detail or reason → a question, an offer or a new time → close.

**Example, a 20-second voicemail saying you will be late (an official sample type; about 32 words):**
*Hej Sara, det är Alex. Förlåt, jag blir ungefär en kvart försenad, eftersom bussen inte har kommit. Jag är där kvart över sex. Kan du vänta på mig vid ingången? Vi ses!*
(Hi Sara, it's Alex. Sorry, I'll be about a quarter of an hour late, because the bus hasn't come. I'll be there at quarter past six. Can you wait for me at the entrance? See you!)

### Engine 4: Opinion (your view, and advice)

**Shape:** view → reason + example → reason → the other side → weigh the two sides → conclusion. For advice: *Jag tycker att du ska …* + a reason + an example.

**Example, a spoken opinion (*Det är bättre att bo i en stad än på landet. Håller du med?*):**
*Jag tycker att det är bättre att bo i en stad. För det första är det lättare att leva utan bil. Till exempel går bussar och tåg ofta. För det andra finns det många jobb i staden. Å andra sidan är det dyrt att bo i en stad. Men för mig är fördelarna större än nackdelarna. Därför tycker jag att det är bättre att bo i en stad.*
(I think it is better to live in a city. First, it is easier to live without a car. For example, buses and trains run often. Second, there are many jobs in the city. On the other hand, it is expensive to live in a city. But for me the advantages are bigger than the disadvantages. That is why I think it is better to live in a city.)

**Weigh before you conclude.** A *Därför* straight after a disadvantage does not follow from it. Say which side wins for you (*Men för mig är fördelarna större än nackdelarna.*), then conclude.

**Develop, don't stop at the tick.** In opinion and story tasks the checklist is the minimum. Give each reason an example and a link word:
- Bare: *Jag tycker att det är bättre att bo i en stad. Det är lättare utan bil.* (I think it is better to live in a city. It is easier without a car.)
- Developed: *Jag tycker att det är bättre att bo i en stad, eftersom det är lättare att leva utan bil. Till exempel går bussarna ofta, så jag kan ta bussen till jobbet varje dag.* (I think it is better to live in a city, because it is easier to live without a car. For example, the buses run often, so I can take the bus to work every day.)

In speaking, two developed reasons are enough. A letter to the editor (an official sample type) opens with the topic (*Jag vill skriva om …*) and needs at least three reasons (*För det tredje …*).

### Engine 5: Describe (a person, a habit, a place, something you sell)

**Shape:** what or who → two details → what I usually do → why it matters. As a seller: age, condition, price, a time to come, your address.

**Example, a talk about a person important to you (an official sample type):**
*Jag vill berätta om min vän Ravi. Vi har känt varandra i femton år. Ravi är lång och har kort svart hår. Vi brukar prata i telefon en gång i veckan. Han är viktig för mig eftersom han alltid finns där när jag behöver honom.*
(I want to tell you about my friend Ravi. We have known each other for fifteen years. Ravi is tall and has short black hair. We usually talk on the phone once a week. He is important to me because he is always there when I need him.)

This is the core of a 1.5-minute talk (about 45 words, so about a third of the time); develop each point (section 2, engine 4) until the time is used.

### Engine 6: Story (what happened, and reports)

**Shape:** when and where → first, then, in the end → how it felt → now. For a report to an office or the police, add a description and your contact details.

**Example, a message explaining why you were late:**
*Hej Sara! Förlåt att jag kom så sent i går. Först kom bussen för sent, och sedan missade jag tåget. Till slut tog jag en taxi, men det var mycket trafik. Det var jobbigt, eftersom jag ville vara med från början. Kram, Alex*
(Hi Sara! Sorry I came so late yesterday. First the bus came too late, and then I missed the train. In the end I took a taxi, but there was a lot of traffic. It was hard, because I wanted to be there from the start. Hugs, Alex)

sections.title: 3. The seven official sample tasks: what each must contain
sections.markdown:
Tick each point. In practice a forgotten point makes the task Amber (section 14); the booking gate (plan 4.7) needs every point.

1. **Talk about a person important to you** (speaking: 1 minute to prepare, 1.5 minutes to talk). The plan's six points: who; how long you have known them; looks and personality; what you do together; why they matter; a memory or a wish.
2. **A buyer phones about your "for sale" ad** (speaking: turns of about 10–25 seconds). Answer the questions (still for sale? age? condition? price? a lower offer?), suggest a time and say where you live.
3. **You phone a repair firm about something still broken** (speaking: 6 turns). Who you are; what is broken; that it is still broken after a repair visit, and when; a protest with a reason; what you want (a new time, your address).
4. **A voicemail saying you will be late** (speaking: 20 seconds). Who you are; that you will be late; a short reason; when you will be there.
5. **An e-mail to a friend about an event** (writing). What; when; where; two more details; a proper opening and closing. The plan adds an invitation question (*Vill du följa med?*).
6. **A letter to the editor** (writing). The topic; your opinion; at least three reasons. The plan adds an example, the other side and a conclusion that matches your opinion.
7. **A complaint about a bill** (writing, formal). Which bill (number, date and amount); at least two reasons why it is too high; an amount you think is fair; your contact details; a formal opening and closing.

sections.title: 4. Openings and closings: they depend on the situation
sections.markdown:
| Situation | Open | Close |
|---|---|---|
| Phone call | *Hej, det här är [namn]. Jag ringer angående [___].* (Hi, this is … I'm calling about …) | *Okej, då säger vi [torsdag klockan tio].* (OK, then we'll say Thursday at ten; only to confirm what you heard.) *Tack för hjälpen. Hej då!* (Thanks for the help. Bye!) |
| Informal e-mail or message | *Hej [namn]!* (Hi …!) | *Hälsningar, [namn]* (Regards, …) |
| Formal e-mail or letter | *Hej! Jag skriver angående [___].* (Hi! I am writing about …; *om* works too) | *Ni når mig på [telefonnummer] eller [e-postadress]. Med vänliga hälsningar, [för- och efternamn]* (You can reach me on … or … Kind regards, …) |
| Opinion (talk or text) | *Jag tycker att [___].* (I think that …) | *Därför tycker jag att [___].* (That is why I think that …) |
| Story or describe (talk) | *Jag vill berätta om [___].* (I want to tell you about …) | *Det var allt jag ville säga.* (That was all I wanted to say.) |
| Face-to-face request | *Ursäkta, kan du [___]?* (Excuse me, can you …?) More polite: *skulle du kunna* | *Tack!* (Thanks!) |
| Reacting to news | *Vad roligt!* (How nice!) / *Vad tråkigt att höra!* (I'm sorry to hear that!) | A question or an offer (section 7) |

*Hej!* is the default formal opening. *Bästa mottagare,* is a reference alternative (section 13).

Never open a hobby talk with a phone greeting, and never close it with a formal letter closing.

sections.title: 5. The core frames (about 60)
sections.markdown:
About 60 frame cards. A few cards hold two sentences (the seller lines, the advice line); on the day you learn them, each sentence counts as one new pattern (load rule 1, section 14). Lines in several groups are listed once per group (see "The counts overlap" at the top).

**Me (6)**
- *Jag heter [___].* (My name is …)
- *Jag kommer från [___].* (I come from …)
- *Jag bor i [___].* (I live in …)
- *Jag talar [___].* (I speak …)
- *Jag lär mig svenska.* (I am learning Swedish.)
- *Jag jobbar som [___].* (I work as …)

**Phone frame (4) and letter frame (5):** in section 4.

**Ask (6)**
- *Jag skulle vilja [boka en tid].* (I would like to book an appointment.)
- *Har ni en ledig tid [på tisdag]?* (Do you have a free time on Tuesday?)
- *Passar det [på torsdag klockan tio]?* (Does Thursday at ten suit you?)
- *Hur mycket kostar [besöket]?* (How much does the visit cost?)
- *Jag undrar om [det finns lediga platser].* (I wonder if there are free places.)
- *När kan jag [komma]?* (When can I come?)

**Fix (8)**
- *[Den] är fortfarande trasig.* (It is still broken.)
- *Problemet är att [den inte startar].* (The problem is that it doesn't start.)
- *En reparatör var här [i tisdags], men det hjälpte inte.* (A repair person was here last Tuesday, but it didn't help.)
- *Kan ni [komma i morgon eller på torsdag]?* (Can you come tomorrow or on Thursday?)
- *Jag vill [få pengarna tillbaka].* (I want to get my money back.)
- *Fakturan är för hög av två skäl.* (The bill is too high, for two reasons.)
- *Jag tycker att [___] euro är ett rimligt belopp.* (I think … euros is a reasonable amount.)
- *Ursäkta, skulle du kunna [prata lite tystare]?* (Excuse me, could you talk a bit more quietly?)

**Social (7)**
- *Tack för [inbjudan].* (Thanks for the invitation.)
- *Tyvärr kan jag inte [komma], eftersom [jag jobbar].* (Unfortunately I can't come, because I'm working.)
- *Kan vi ses [på lördag] i stället?* (Can we meet on Saturday instead?)
- *Förlåt, jag blir [en kvart] försenad, eftersom [___].* (Sorry, I'll be a quarter of an hour late, because …)
- *Jag är där [kvart över sex].* (I'll be there at quarter past six.)
- *Det är [på lördag] klockan [___] [i/på ___].* (It is on Saturday at … in/at …)
- *Vill du [följa med]?* (Do you want to come along?)

**Opinion (8)**
- *Jag tycker att [___].* (I think that …)
- *Jag håller med.* / *Jag håller inte med.* (I agree. / I don't agree.)
- *För det första [___]. För det andra [___]. För det tredje [___].* (First … Second … Third … The verb comes next: *För det första sparar man tid.*)
- *Till exempel [___].* (For example …)
- *Å andra sidan [___].* (On the other hand …)
- *Men för mig är fördelarna större än nackdelarna.* (But for me the advantages are bigger than the disadvantages. Say it before the conclusion.)
- *Därför tycker jag att [___].* (That is why I think that …)
- *Jag tycker att du ska [___]. Du kan till exempel [___].* (I think you should … You can for example … For advice.)

**Describe (11)**
- A person:
  - *Jag vill berätta om [___].* (I want to tell you about …)
  - *Hon är [snäll och glad].* (She is kind and cheerful.)
  - *Jag har känt henne [i tio år].* (I have known her for ten years.)
  - *Vi brukar [laga mat tillsammans].* (We usually cook together.)
  - *Hon är viktig för mig eftersom [___].* (She is important to me because …)
- A habit, a place or a thing:
  - *Jag brukar [simma två gånger i veckan].* (I usually swim twice a week.)
  - *Det finns [en bastu och en brygga].* (There is a sauna and a jetty.)
  - *Den ligger [nära centrum].* (It is near the centre. With an *ett*-word: *Det ligger …*)
- Something you sell:
  - *Ja, den finns kvar. Den är [tre] år gammal och i bra skick.* (Yes, it's still for sale. It is three years old and in good condition.)
  - *Den kostar [150] euro, men du kan få den för [130] euro.* (It costs 150 euros, but you can have it for 130.)
  - *Du kan komma [i morgon efter klockan sex]. Jag bor på [Solvägen 5] i [Esbo].* (You can come tomorrow after six. I live at Solvägen 5 in Espoo.)

**Story (5)**
- *[Förra veckan] hände något [konstigt].* (Last week something strange happened.)
- *Först [___]. Sedan [___]. Till slut [___].* (First … Then … In the end … The verb comes next after each.)
- *Det var [jobbigt], eftersom [___].* (It was hard, because …)
- *Jag har tappat bort [min plånbok].* (I have lost my wallet.)
- *Det hände [i går kväll] [på bussen].* (It happened last night on the bus.)

For a report, borrow *Kan ni [kontakta mig]?* (Can you contact me?) from Fix.

sections.title: 6. Twelve reason pairs
sections.markdown:
Each pair has a "for" and an "against" side, so you can argue either way. Follow a reason with *Till exempel …* and a detail from the task. Use only reasons that fit.

| Topic | For (the positive side) | Against (the negative side) |
|---|---|---|
| Time | *Det sparar tid.* (It saves time.) | *Det tar mycket tid.* (It takes a lot of time.) |
| Cost | *Det är billigare.* (It is cheaper.) | *Det är dyrt.* (It is expensive.) |
| Health | *Det är bra för hälsan.* (It is good for your health.) | *Man rör sig för lite.* (You move too little.) |
| Environment | *Det är bra för miljön.* (It is good for the environment.) | *Det är dåligt för miljön.* (It is bad for the environment.) |
| Stress | *Man blir mindre stressad.* (You get less stressed.) | *Man blir lätt stressad.* (You easily get stressed.) |
| People | *Man träffar nya människor.* (You meet new people.) | *Man kan känna sig ensam.* (You can feel lonely.) |
| Safety | *Det är tryggt.* (It feels safe.) | *Det kan vara farligt.* (It can be dangerous.) |
| Choice | *Man kan välja själv.* (You can choose yourself.) | *Det passar inte alla.* (It does not suit everyone.) |
| Ease | *Det gör vardagen enklare.* (It makes everyday life easier.) | *Det kan vara svårt för äldre människor.* (It can be hard for older people.) |
| Children | *Det är bra för barnen.* (It is good for the children.) | *Barnen sitter för mycket framför skärmen.* (Children sit too much in front of the screen.) |
| Quality | *Kvaliteten är ofta bättre.* (The quality is often better.) | *Servicen blir sämre.* (The service gets worse.) |
| Flexibility | *Man kan göra det när som helst.* (You can do it at any time.) | *Det kan bli fel.* (Things can go wrong.) |

*man* means "you" or "people in general". After *En nackdel är att* (a disadvantage is that), *inte* moves before the verb: *En nackdel är att det inte passar alla.*

sections.title: 7. Ten reactions
sections.markdown:
Shape: react → one detail → a question, an offer or a close. [bank N] is the plan's number. Example: *Grattis! Vad roligt att du har fått jobbet! När börjar du?* (Congratulations! How nice that you got the job! When do you start?)

1. *Grattis! Vad roligt!* (Congratulations! How nice!) [bank 1]
2. *Vad tråkigt att höra.* (I'm sorry to hear that.) [bank 6]
3. *Krya på dig!* (Get well soon! Only for illness.) [bank 8]
4. *Jag beklagar sorgen.* (I'm sorry for your loss. Only for a death.) [bank 12]
5. *Tack så mycket för hjälpen!* (Thank you very much for the help!) [bank 14]
6. *Det gör inget.* (It doesn't matter. The reply to an apology.) [bank 19]
7. *Förlåt att jag är sen.* (Sorry I'm late. When you are already late.) [bank 22]
8. *Förlåt, jag blir lite sen.* (Sorry, I'll be a bit late. Before the meeting time.) [bank 23]
9. *Ja, gärna!* (Yes, please! / Yes, I'd like to! A warm yes to an offer or an invitation.) [bank 25]
10. *Tyvärr kan jag inte.* (Unfortunately I can't.) [bank 28]

sections.title: 8. Eight rescue phrases
sections.markdown:
Never go silent, and never switch to English.

1. *Förlåt, jag menar …* (Sorry, I mean … Correct yourself once, then carry on.)
2. *Jag säger det på ett annat sätt.* (I'll say it another way.)
3. *Jag kommer inte på ordet, men det är något man använder för att …* (I can't think of the word, but it's something you use to … For example, if *bromsarna* (the brakes) is the missing word: *… något man använder för att stanna.* (… something you use to stop.) Describe the use with words you know.)
4. *Det är som en …* (It's like a …)
5. *Jag är inte säker, men jag tror att …* (I'm not sure, but I think that …)
6. *Det beror på …* (It depends on …)
7. *Till exempel …* (For example …)
8. *Det var allt jag ville säga.* (That was all I wanted to say.)

**If you miss what the recorded voice said.** You cannot ask it to repeat. Choose one of three moves:
1. **You understood all of it:** answer it.
2. **You understood part of it:** answer that part.
3. **You missed it:** give a relevant point from your card, without agreeing to anything: *Jag kan komma på fredag efter klockan fyra.* (I can come on Friday after four.)

Do not say *okej* or *ja* by reflex: it can agree to something you did not hear.

sections.title: 9. Thirty verbs, in three steps
sections.markdown:
**Step 1: the present of all 30** (base form → present).

*vara → är* (be), *ha → har* (have), *göra → gör* (do, make), *gå → går* (go, walk), *komma → kommer* (come), *åka → åker* (go, travel), *få → får* (get, may), *ta → tar* (take), *ge → ger* (give), *se → ser* (see), *säga → säger* (say), *veta → vet* (know), *kunna → kan* (can), *vilja → vill* (want), *bli → blir* (become, get), *köpa → köper* (buy), *betala → betalar* (pay), *ringa → ringer* (phone), *skicka → skickar* (send), *boka → bokar* (book), *jobba → jobbar* (work), *bo → bor* (live), *träffa → träffar* (meet), *fungera → fungerar* (work, of a thing), *hjälpa → hjälper* (help), *skriva → skriver* (write), *äta → äter* (eat), *sova → sover* (sleep), *glömma → glömmer* (forget), *tycka → tycker* (think, an opinion).

**Step 2: the past of 12.** *var* (was), *köpte* (bought), *ringde* (phoned), *kom* (came), *glömde* (forgot), *gick* (went), *hjälpte* (helped), *tog* (took), *blev* (became, got), *fick* (got), *sa* (said), *bodde* (lived). Use the past with a finished time: *Jag köpte den i måndags.* (I bought it last Monday.) Phase 1 teaches only 5 of them, in sentences: *var, kom, gick* (Day 6) and *ringde, köpte* (Day 9). The other 7 come in Phase 2: *tog, glömde, blev, hjälpte* on Day 34a, and *fick, sa, bodde* from the plan's verb table (2.9) when a task needs them.

**The future** (plan 2.9, G8) is library material in Phase 1, with one exception: Day 9 learns *ska* + base form as a chunk: *I morgon ska jag ringa till banken.* (Tomorrow I'm going to call the bank.)

**Step 3: the perfect, only inside chunks.** Learn these whole: *Jag har bott i Finland i fem år.* (I have lived in Finland for five years.) / *Jag har redan betalat.* (I have already paid.) / *Har ni fått mitt mejl?* (Have you got my e-mail?)

---

sections.title: 10. Words to recognise on the task card
sections.markdown:
**Instruction words (23):** *läs* (read), *lyssna* (listen), *välj* (choose), *skriv* (write), *svara* (answer), *fråga* (ask), *berätta* (tell), *förklara* (explain), *beskriv* (describe), *jämför* (compare), *föreslå* (suggest), *motivera* (give reasons for), *rätt / fel* (true / false), *åtminstone* (at least), *minst* (at least: *minst tre skäl*, at least three reasons), *ange* (state, give: *Ange ditt telefonnummer.*), *be om* (ask for: *Be om en ny tid.*), *ställ två frågor* (ask two questions), *ge exempel* (give examples), *nämn* (name, mention), *ta ställning* (take a position: say whether you agree), *för- och nackdelar* (advantages and disadvantages), *lämna ett meddelande* (leave a message).

**Two lists, not one.** These 23 are the full recognition list. Days 1–13 teach 20 of them; the other 3 (*ge exempel, ta ställning, för- och nackdelar*) are proposed for the opinion days (Days 29–31b). The Day 14 word test (E1) is a separate list of exactly 41 words: the 20 instruction words met by Day 13, the 11 question words below, and 10 meaning-flip words (*inte* not, *tyvärr* unfortunately, *i stället* instead, *stängt* closed, *men* but, *inställd* cancelled, *försenad* delayed, *redan* already, *flyttad* moved, *ändrad* changed).

**Question words (11):** *vem* (who), *vad* (what), *var* (where), *när* (when), *hur* (how), *hur mycket* (how much), *hur många* (how many), *hur länge* (how long), *hur ofta* (how often), *varför* (why), *vilken / vilket / vilka* (which).

**The question-to-answer reflex.** Hear the question word, know what the answer must hold. The table is built up from Day 2 (three rows), one row on the day each question word is taught; *Vad hände?* comes in Phase 2 (Day 34a). The full set:

| Question | Your answer gives, and how it starts |
|---|---|
| *Var?* | a place: *I [Esbo]. / På [jobbet].* |
| *När?* | a time: *På [fredag]. / Klockan [tio].* |
| *Varför?* | a reason: *Eftersom [jag jobbar].* |
| *Hur mycket?* | a price or amount: *[Sextio] euro.* |
| *Hur länge?* | a duration: *I [två år]. / Sedan [maj].* |
| *Vad tycker du?* | an opinion: *Jag tycker att [___].* |
| *Vad hände?* | a past event: *[I går] hände något [oväntat].* (Yesterday something unexpected happened.) |
| *Vad vill du?* | a request: *Jag skulle vilja [___].* |

sections.title: 11. One answer, several questions
sections.markdown:
Learn one answer; recognise the different ways the question can be asked. The curriculum adds these a few at a time in Phase 1.

- *Jag bor i Esbo.* answers *Var bor du?* / *Var bor du nu?* / *I vilken stad bor du?* / *Var någonstans bor du?* (Where do you live? / … now? / In which town …? / Whereabouts …?)
- *Jag kommer från Indien.* answers *Var kommer du ifrån?* / *Varifrån kommer du?* / *Vilket land kommer du från?* (Where are you from? / … / Which country are you from?)
- *Jag heter Alex.* answers *Vad heter du?* / *Vad är ditt namn?* (What is your name?)

---

sections.title: 12. The substitution bank: start verb + action
sections.markdown:
A look-up table, not a list to memorise. Take a start verb, add an action in the base form (no *att*), and make it positive, negative or a question.

| Start verb | Yes | No (*inte* after the start verb) | Question (start verb first) |
|---|---|---|---|
| *kan* (can) | *Jag kan [komma].* | *Jag kan inte [komma].* | *Kan du [komma]?* |
| *vill* (want to) | *Jag vill [komma].* | *Jag vill inte [komma].* | *Vill du [komma]?* |
| *måste* (must, have to) | *Jag måste [jobba hemma].* | *Jag måste inte [jobba hemma].* | *Måste du [jobba hemma]?* |
| *ska* (am going to) | *Jag ska [ringa].* | *Jag ska inte [ringa].* | *Ska du [ringa]?* |
| *brukar* (usually) | *Jag brukar [jobba hemma].* | *Jag brukar inte [jobba hemma].* | *Brukar du [jobba hemma]?* |

**Ten actions for the gap:** *komma* (come), *ringa* (phone), *jobba hemma* (work at home), *boka en tid* (book an appointment), *betala med kort* (pay by card), *träffa dig* (meet you), *hjälpa dig* (help you), *skicka ett mejl* (send an e-mail), *åka till jobbet* (go to work), *köpa en ny* (buy a new one).

- *måste inte* means "don't have to" (*behöver inte* says the same). For "must not", say *får inte*: *Du får inte parkera här.* (You must not park here.)
- With a time first, the start verb is still second: *I morgon kan jag inte komma.* (I can't come tomorrow.)
- Not every pairing makes sense (*Jag brukar köpa en ny*); use the ones that do.

sections.title: 13. Techniques and alternatives (no new lines to learn)
sections.markdown:
**Concept words: a way to find a reason fast.** Ask what the statement touches: *tid* (time), *pengar* (money), *hälsa* (health), *miljö* (environment), *trygghet* (safety), *människor* (people), *barn* (children), *arbete* (work), *frihet* (freedom), *stress*, *kvalitet* (quality), *problem*. Then take the matching pair in section 6. Working from home? *tid* and *stress*: *Det sparar tid. Man blir mindre stressad.*

**Sentence families.** Learn a sentence with 2–3 variants, never a verb as a four-form table.
- Time, money, work: *Det tar mycket tid.* (It takes a lot of time.) / *Det kostar mycket pengar.* (It costs a lot of money.) / *Det är mycket arbete.* (It is a lot of work.)
- Yesterday, today, tomorrow: *I går jobbade jag hemma.* (Yesterday I worked at home.) / *I dag jobbar jag hemma.* (Today I'm working at home.) / *I morgon ska jag jobba hemma.* (Tomorrow I'm going to work at home.) Up to now: *Jag har jobbat hemma i två år.* (I have worked at home for two years.)
- With a future time word, the present works too: *På måndag jobbar jag hemma.* or *På måndag ska jag jobba hemma.* (On Monday I'm working at home.)

**Word recovery** (the long form of rescue phrases 3 and 4): *Det är en sak som [___].* (It's a thing that …) / *Det är en plats där [___].* (It's a place where …) / *Det är en person som [___].* (It's a person who …) / *Man använder den för att [___].* (You use it to …) / *Det är ungefär som [___].* (It's roughly like …)

**Formal opening, alternative.** *Bästa mottagare,* (Dear recipient,) is used in Finland in formal letters. *Hej!* (section 4) is the default and is always safe.

---

sections.title: 14. The nine daily load rules, and when to move on
sections.markdown:
1. **At most 6 new patterns and 8 new cards a day.** Count patterns, not bullets or cards: a pattern is one sentence shape you can recall on its own. A card that holds 2–3 sentences counts as 2–3 patterns. A pattern you already know, or a simple swap of a detail in it, is not new.
2. One grammar point a day, stated in one sentence.
3. Review stops at 8 minutes, finished or not.
4. Hear each new line before saying it.
5. One speaking task and one typed task. A book task replaces the day's own prompt.
6. A day is 60 minutes. If a block is added, another is removed.
7. A day is done when a changed version of the task works, not when a list is recited fast.
8. Mark the day Green, Amber or Red (below). Only Red repeats the skill tomorrow, with new details.
9. If a day holds more than rule 1 allows, split it into day a and day b. Day b uses the same tasks with new details.

**Listening and reading every day.** A 60-minute day gives 8 minutes to Finland-Swedish listening or reading, and a 90-minute day gives 10 (plan section 7). Light, mock and test days set their own amount, and their day entry says how much.

**Green, Amber, Red.**
- **Green, move on:** you understood the task and gave every required point on your own (the model only to check afterwards).
- **Amber, move on with revision:** understandable, but you hesitated, repeated a mistake or forgot a point. Put the top 1–2 mistakes on the error list and revisit them later. Do not repeat the day.
- **Red, repeat the skill tomorrow with new details:** you misunderstood the question, could not answer, or needed the model to answer.
- **Borderline cases.** A forgotten required point (contact details, an amount) in ordinary practice is Amber, unless the message cannot be used without it; then it is Red. Small grammar slips, or a wrong tense the listener still understands (*I går ringer jag till banken.*, present for past), are Amber or Green, never Red on their own.
- Counts (errors, words, seconds, "4 of 5") are targets, never gates. Spelling and capitals never make a task Amber or Red if the message is clear. Only the plan's booking gate (4.7) is a fixed test, and it needs every required point.

**Time pressure grows step by step.** First hearing and repeating: no timer. Saying it from the English: gentle (double the target time). Changing the sentence: moderate. A question you have not practised: exam-like. Mocks: full exam conditions.

**The transfer test for any new sentence** (*Jag bor i Esbo.*): 1 recall it from the English; 2 swap a detail (*i Vanda*); 3 change the person (*Hon bor i Vanda.*); 4 understand the question it answers (*Var bor du?*); 5 build that question yourself from the statement (*Jag bor i Esbo.* → *Var bor du?*; *Och du?* is a useful move too, but it does not test this); 6 understand it spoken; 7 type it.

**Active recall.**
- **Cover and say:** cover the Swedish, read the English, say the Swedish aloud, then uncover and check. A miss comes back tomorrow.
- **Swap drill:** say one frame three times with a new detail each time: *Kan vi ses [på lördag] i stället?* → *på söndag*, *i morgon*, *efter jobbet*.

sections.title: 15. The first two days
sections.markdown:
`YKI-LEARNER-DAYS-1-14.md` is the full version of these days; where it differs from this summary, the learner pages win.

### Day 1: say who you are

**New frames (5):** *Jag heter [Alex].* (My name is …) / *Jag kommer från [Indien].* (I come from …) / *Jag bor i [Esbo].* (I live in …) / *Jag talar [engelska, hindi och marathi].* (I speak …) / *Jag lär mig svenska.* (I am learning Swedish.)

**Questions to understand (4):** *Vad heter du?* (What is your name?) / *Var kommer du ifrån?* (Where are you from?) / *Var bor du?* (Where do you live?) / *Vilka språk talar du?* (Which languages do you speak?)

**Instruction words to recognise (2):** *berätta* (tell), *skriv* (write).

**The one grammar fact:** the verb has the same form for every person: *jag bor, du bor*.

**Steps (60 minutes):** hear each frame three times and repeat it (no timer) → cover and say each frame from the English, then swap the detail three times → answer the four questions, mixed, in full sentences → speaking card *Berätta om dig själv.* (Tell about yourself.): record five sentences, listen once, redo once → set up å, ä and ö, and type the five sentences from memory → change check: answer as Sara (from Sweden, lives in Åbo, speaks Swedish and Finnish; the words you need: *Sverige* (Sweden), *Åbo* (Turku), *svenska och finska* (Swedish and Finnish)) → 8 cards; start an error log.

**Model:** *Hej! Jag heter Alex. Jag kommer från Indien. Jag bor i Esbo. Jag talar engelska, hindi och marathi. Jag lär mig svenska.*

**Done when (section 14):** Green if you understand all four questions and answer each in a full sentence without reading. Spelling slips do not count.

### Day 2: say more, and ask back

**New frames (5):** *Jag jobbar som [ingenjör].* (I work as …) / *Jag har bott i Finland i [fem] år.* (I have lived in Finland for … years. Learn it as one piece.) / *Vad heter du?* (now you ask it) / *Var bor du?* (now you ask it) / *Och du?* (And you?)

**Questions to understand (2 more):** *Vad jobbar du med?* (What do you do for work?) / *Hur länge har du bott i Finland?* (How long have you lived in Finland?)

**Numbers 0–12:** *noll, ett, två, tre, fyra, fem, sex, sju, åtta, nio, tio, elva, tolv.*

**Instruction words to recognise (2):** *fråga* (ask), *svara* (answer).

**The one grammar fact:** in a question, the verb comes straight after the question word: *Var bor du?*, not *Var du bor?*

**Steps (60 minutes):** say the Day 1 cards aloud → hear and repeat the frames and numbers 0–12 → turn answers into questions (*Jag bor i Esbo.* → *Var bor du?*), then answer all six questions → speaking: a helper asks about your name, home, work and years in Finland; answer each in one sentence, and twice add *Och du?*; record, listen once, redo once → typing card: *Skriv till en ny kurskamrat. Berätta om dig själv och ställ två frågor.* (Write to a new course-mate. Tell about yourself and ask two questions.) → hear 8 numbers from 0 to 12 and write the digits → at most 8 cards.

**Model:** *Hej! Jag heter Alex och jag kommer från Indien. Jag bor i Esbo. Jag har bott i Finland i fem år. Jag jobbar som ingenjör. Jag lär mig svenska. Vad heter du? Var bor du? Hälsningar, Alex*

**Done when (section 14):** Green if you answer the six questions in full sentences, your own two questions have the verb before *du*, and the message has a greeting, five facts, two questions and a closing.

The minute plans are in the study plan (5.1) and the curriculum.

The nine daily load rules in plan section 1 override any day entry below. sections.title: Week 3 (Phase 2 Task moves)
sections.markdown:
**How Days 15–84 are judged (16 November 2026, second review; plan section 1; Amber and Red made precise by the third review).** Every "Done when" from here on uses this rule instead of counted gates.
- **Green, move on:** you understood the task and gave all its required points on your own. A model was read only afterwards, to check.
- **Amber, move on with revision:** understandable, but you hesitated, made a recurring mistake, or forgot a required point (for example the contact details or an amount) while the message still works. Put the top 1–2 mistakes on the error list and revisit them inside later days. Do not repeat the day.
- **Red, repeat the skill tomorrow with new details:** you misunderstood the card, gave no answer, needed to read the model to answer, or the message cannot be used (for example a complaint that never says what is wrong).
- **Grammar alone never makes a task Red.** A minor slip, or a wrong tense that the listener still understands (*Förra helgen går jag på bio.*), is Green or Amber: log it.
- **Numbers are targets, not gates:** seconds, word counts, error counts and "N of M" in a "Done when" are listed under "Targets (not gates)". Spelling and capital-letter slips never make a task Amber or Red if the message is clear. Engine errors (G1, G2, G3, G5) are counted and kept on the error list.
- **Two exceptions keep their own rule.** The **Phase-exit rule** (Days 41–42 and 62–63): the phase is passed when at most 1 task is Red and no Red is a misunderstood question on a required point; the Red tasks are repeated with new details in the next days, then the phase moves on. The **booking-gate checks** on mock days (Days 28, 56, 84 and every mock after Day 84): record Green, Amber or Red per subtest, plus the gate's own checks (every required point covered, every task in time, a teacher rating of A or B, that is "understandable with some errors" or better; engine errors tracked, not gated).

**Time pressure grows step by step (Days 15–40; plan 3.2).** Hearing new lines, imitating them and the ladder: **no timer**. The first take of the day's own card: a **gentle** timer, double the printed limit (40 s for a 20-second turn). The redo with one changed detail: a **moderate** timer, about one and a half times the limit. The printed limit itself (for example 20 s a turn) is for an **unfamiliar card**: a book task, a card the helper has changed, the exit test on Days 41–42. **Full exam conditions only in the mocks** (Days 28, 56, 84). The printed limits in the entries below are the targets.

**Load, minutes and task habits (third review, 16 November 2026).** [Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]
- **Count patterns, not cards (load rule 1).** A new pattern is a sentence shape you must recall on its own. A card that holds 2 or 3 sentences counts as 2 or 3 patterns. A known pattern with a new word in its slot (a substitution) is not a new pattern, and neither is a pattern mastered on an earlier day. A day holds at most **6 new patterns and 8 new cards**; extra lines are marked **library** (look them up when a card needs them; no card) or named for a later day. Days 16–40, 58–61 and 74–76 end their lesson plan with a **Load check** line: new patterns, new cards, and the minutes estimated from the printed activities.
- **How the minutes are estimated** [Plan's own]: about 30 s to hear a new line and say it three times; 30 s per ladder rung; a 6-turn call about 3 minutes a take and 2 minutes to listen back; a 20 s + 25 s reaction round about 1.5 minutes a take at the gentle timer; a 1 + 1.5 minute talk about 5 minutes a take at the gentle timer and 2 minutes to listen back; writing as printed (the time includes the check).
- **Listening or reading on an ordinary day: 8 minutes on a 60-minute day, 10 on a 90-minute day** (the 48–56 and 72–84 blocks of 3.1). The 8-minute version is the 10-minute routine of 7.3 or 7.4 without its last step, the 2 cards, which you make only if today's card count allows. Only declared exceptions (exit-test, set and mock days) give it less, and they say so (for example "6 minutes"). Light days use the full 10-minute routine.
- **One main engine per task, then borrow.** Read the card, choose the engine that does its main job, then borrow single moves from other engines when the card asks for them. A complaint is Fix, with a short Story (what happened, when) and an Ask (what you want).
- **If you miss the recorded voice's line**, choose one of three: you understood all of it, so answer it; you understood part, so answer that part; you missed it, so give the next piece of task information that fits the card, without agreeing to anything (*Jag kan komma på fredag efter klockan fyra.*). Never say *Okej* by reflex: it can sound as if you agree.
- **Length** [Plan's own]: practise at about 80 words a minute, so 20 s is about 25–33 words, 25 s about 33–40, 1 minute about 80, 1.5 minutes about 120. These are practice aims, not exam rules.
- **Develop, do not just tick.** In opinion and story tasks a ticked checklist is the minimum: join the points with a reason, an example and a link word instead of giving the shortest answer. In calls and messages, stop once every point is covered. Bare: *Jag tycker att det är bra. Det sparar tid.* Developed: *Jag tycker att det är bra att handla på nätet, eftersom det sparar tid. Till exempel behöver jag inte åka till affären efter jobbet, så jag har mer tid med familjen.*

# YKI level 3 exam-first curriculum, part 2: Days 29–56

[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]

This part covers Days 29–56: the second half of Phase 2 (task moves, Days 29–42, ending with the Phase 2 exit test on Days 41–42) and the first two weeks of Phase 3 (topic transfer, Days 43–56, ending with Mock 2 on Day 56).

sections.title: Overview
sections.markdown:
*Written November 2026 for one adult learner. Everything needed is inside this document.*

**Read this first.**

- **All Swedish in this plan is unreviewed.** A Swedish teacher must check every Swedish line before you drill it. Each Swedish block carries the tag **[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]** as a reminder.
- **This plan cannot guarantee a result.** Only official YKI raters give grades.
- **"The research"** means a November 2026 summary of official pages from OPH, JYU and Migri, a handful of test-takers' accounts, and one practice book. Every tagged fact below comes from it.
- **Every exam fact carries a tag that says where it comes from:**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[Official]** | Stated by OPH (the Finnish National Agency for Education, which runs YKI), the University of Jyväskylä (JYU, which develops the tests and trains raters), or Migri (the Finnish Immigration Service). |
| **[Official sample]** | From JYU's public practice tasks. These are paper-era and undated, and are not real test tasks. They show the task types; your sitting may differ. |
| **[Teacher, unofficial]** | A Swedish class teacher's description of the exam format. Useful practice targets, not rules. |
| **[Book count]** | Counted by hand from one published Swedish YKI practice book (225 tasks; Gimara). This is one author's selection, not an official task bank, and the counts are about ±10%. |
| **[Plan's own]** | A benchmark or limit invented for this plan. |
| **[Unknown]** | Not published, or not found. |

> **Freeze and pilot (third review, 16 November 2026).** The architecture is frozen: the six engines, the three-layer core, the load rules, Green/Amber/Red, the phase map and the booking gate stay as they are. Start Days 1–7 now and fill in `YKI-PILOT-LOG.md` every day. Revise the plan from what the log shows (real minutes, next-day recall, what was too much), one change at a time, not from more reviews.

> **Decisions (16 November 2026)**, made after the audit adjudication (`archive/YKI-AUDIT-ADJUDICATION.md`, now a historical record):
>
> 1. **Core and library.** The core has three layers (since the third review; `YKI-CORE-SHEET.md`). The **active core** is what you recall and use without notes: 6 engines (answer shapes), about 60 sentence frames, the openings and closings for each situation (section 1; the phone and letter frames are two of them), the 7 official-sample checklists, 12 reason pairs, 10 reactions, 8 rescue phrases and 30 verbs in three steps. The **recognition core** is what you only need to understand: 23 instruction words, 11 question words and common ways of asking the same question. The **reference** layer (a substitution bank and a few techniques) is looked up, never memorised. Templates T1–T20, the banks and the 84 day entries are a **reference library**; the T-numbers stay as aliases. The 84-day calendar is a default order: you move on by the load rules in section 1, not by date, so Phase 1 may take about 15 study days (14, plus the Day 3 split) and more if Reds need repeating.
> 2. **Fresh mock prompts.** The mocks that count towards booking use prompts the teacher writes, or, as the fallback, prompts an AI writes on the day (6.2). Everything printed in this plan, the curriculum and the appendix is **seen practice**, and since the third review so are the 40 held-back book tasks: their descriptions were printed in the learner's book map until the second review, and the book is the learner's own. They stay in `teacher-only/YKI-MOCK-RESERVE.md` (with the mock recipe and the gap table, for the teacher or the helper; the learner does not open it) and serve Mocks 1 and 2 and spare practice.
> 3. **Where the core lives.** In these documents for now. Audio comes from the teacher and the book's QR tracks. Building the core into an app is for later and not yet decided.
> 4. **Second review (16 November 2026).** You move on by **Green, Amber or Red** (section 1); counts are targets, and only the booking gate (4.7) stays a fixed test. Time pressure grows step by step (3.2). Openings and closings follow the situation, not the engine (section 1). Five techniques make the core flexible without new lines to learn: the question-to-answer reflex (2.6), opinion concept words (2.4), word recovery (2.8), sentence families (2.9) and the transfer test (3.2). T20 is optional library material. Listening and reading get search strategy too (section 7), but strategy does not replace comprehension.
> 5. **Third review (16 November 2026).** Load rule 1 counts patterns, not cards. Green, Amber and Red have borderline rules (a forgotten point is Amber unless the message is unusable). Each task has one main engine that borrows moves from the others. A missed recorded line has three recovery moves, and no automatic *Okej*. Answers are paced at about 80 words a minute (2.1). Opinion and story answers are developed, not stopped at the first tick (2.8). The recognition list holds 23 instruction words (2.6). The listening and reading minimum is 8 minutes on a 60-minute day and 10 minutes on a 90-minute day (section 7). Counted mocks use teacher-written or AI-on-the-day prompts only (6.2).
>
> `YKI-CORE-SHEET.md` holds the whole core on one sheet, with English, in its three layers.

sections.title: 1. Summary, the core and the daily load rules
sections.markdown:
### The goal

The goal is level 3 (CEFR B1) on the **Swedish YKI intermediate test**, in a subtest pair that Migri accepts for Finnish citizenship. Reach it as fast as you honestly can, without learning all of Swedish.

### The method in 8 lines

1. **Measure first.** A timed Day 0 placement decides which phase you start in.
2. **Learn the exam's task types** and the language moves ("functions") they need, not the whole language.
3. **Memorise one small core for both speaking and writing** ("The core", below): six answer shapes, about 60 sentence frames, 12 reason pairs, 10 reactions and 8 rescue phrases. The 20 slot templates and the banks in section 2 are a library to look things up in.
4. **Learn a small grammar "engine"** that prevents level-2 errors: verb in second place, the place of *inte*, *att*-clauses, questions, modal verbs and past forms.
5. **Practise with the substitution ladder:** hear it first, then say a sentence, swap a detail, add a reason, add a solution, change it, then produce it from memory for a new prompt.
6. **Every day, do one timed speaking task** (recorded) and **one typed writing task**, each checked against a list of required points.
7. **Every study day, spend 8 minutes (on a 60-minute day) or 10 minutes (on a 90-minute day)** on Finland-Swedish listening or reading, so the other subtest pairs stay open. Light, mock and test days set their own amount (section 7).
8. **A teacher rates your work every week.** Day to day you move on by Green, Amber or Red (below); counts are targets. The booking gate uses the teacher's rating plus things you can check. You book an exam only on evidence, never on hope.

### The core and the reference library (decided 16 November 2026)

**The rule.** The core has three layers (`YKI-CORE-SHEET.md`): the **active core** you recall and use without notes, the **recognition core** you only need to understand when you hear or read it, and a small **reference** layer you look up. Your memorising time goes to the active core. Everything else in this plan is the reference library: you look it up when a task needs it.

| Item | Count | Where it is |
|---|---|---|
| Engines (answer shapes) | 6 | The table below: a new grouping of T1–T20 |
| Openings and closings | by situation (7 kinds); the phone and letter frames are two of them | The table under the engines below; 2.0 (from T1, T5 and T6) |
| Official-sample checklists | 7 | The speaking and writing samples under "What is known about the exam"; the required points in T5 and T6 (2.3) |
| Sentence frames | about 60 | 2.0 |
| Reason pairs | 12 pairs (24 lines) | 2.4, by number: 1/22 time, 3/21 cost, 4/28 health, 5/24 environment, 16/26 stress, 10/33 people, 13/25 safety, 8/36 choice, 7/23 ease, 14/34 children, 19/40 quality, 17/37 flexibility |
| Reactions | 10 | 2.5, numbers 1, 6, 8, 12, 14, 19, 22, 23, 25, 28 (19 is the reply to an apology, 25 a warm yes to an offer or an invitation) |
| Rescue phrases | 8 | 2.8, unchanged |
| Verbs | 30, in three steps | G6 in 2.9: the present of all 30 first; then the past of 12, of which Phase 1 teaches 5 (*var, kom, gick* on Day 6; *ringde, köpte* on Day 9) and Phase 2 the other 7 (*tog, glömde, blev, hjälpte* on Day 34a; *fick, sa, bodde* from the library); the perfect only inside chunks |
| Instruction and question words | 23 + 11, recognition core (understand, not produce) | 2.6 |

The counts overlap: some lines sit in two groups (*Jag tycker att …* is a frame and the opinion opening; *Till exempel …* is a frame and a rescue phrase), so the numbers are not a count of unique sentences to add up.

**The six engines.** An engine is the shape of an answer. Pick one **main** engine from the task card and fill it with the card's details; then borrow single moves from the other engines when the card asks for them (third review). A complaint about a repair, for example, runs on Fix, borrows the Story sequence for what happened (*Först … Sedan …*) and an Ask line for the new time (*Har ni en ledig tid på torsdag?*). The engine does not decide how you open and close: the situation does (the openings table below). **[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

| Engine | Shape | Old IDs (now aliases) | Book tasks (of 225) [Book count] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Ask | who I am → what I want → one or two questions → confirm → thanks | T2, T3 buyer, T20e | request 40 |
| 2. Fix | what is wrong → since when → why it matters → what I want → close | T4, T5, T17, T20c, T20d | complaint 33 |
| 3. Social | react or say the news → one detail or reason → question, offer or new time → close | T6–T10, T20a, thanks and notice from T16 | react, refusal, apology, invitation 34 |
| 4. Opinion | view → reason + example → reason → other side → conclusion. For advice: "I think you should …" + reason + example | T13, T11, T19 | opinion 52, advice 13 |
| 5. Describe | what or who → two details → what I usually do → why it matters. Seller role: age, condition, price, time, address | T14, T18, T3 seller, T20b, directions and appearance from T16 | describe 25 |
| 6. Story | when and where → first, then, in the end → how it felt → now. For a report: add a description and contact details | T15, T12 | tell 13, report 13 |

All 12 book functions have a home; advice sits in Opinion, where its shape fits. **What is lost:** one memorised line per rare situation (resigning, giving things away), which is 6 of 225 book tasks. Look those up in T20 when the book task comes; T20 is optional library material, not a compulsory early block (second review, 16 November 2026).

**Openings and closings depend on the situation, not on the engine** (second review, 16 November 2026). Most lines are already core frames (2.0); the rest are short and come from the reaction bank.

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

| Situation | Open | Close |
|---|---|---|
| Phone call | *Hej, det här är [namn].* (Hi, this is …) | *Tack för hjälpen. Hej då!* (Thanks for the help. Bye!) |
| Informal e-mail or message | *Hej!* or *Hej [namn]!* | *Hälsningar, [namn]* (Regards, …) |
| Formal e-mail | *Hej! Jag skriver angående [___].* (Hi! I am writing about …; *om* also works) | *Med vänliga hälsningar, [namn]* (Kind regards, …), after your contact details |
| Opinion (talk or text) | *Jag tycker att [___].* (I think that …) | *Därför tycker jag att [___].* (That is why I think that …) |
| Story or describe (talk) | *Jag vill berätta om [___].* (I want to tell you about …) | Why it matters, or *Det var allt jag ville säga.* (rescue phrase 8) |
| Face-to-face request | *Ursäkta, kan du [___]?* (Excuse me, can you …?) More polite: *skulle du kunna* | *Tack!* |
| Reacting to news | *Vad roligt!* (How nice!) / *Vad tråkigt att höra!* (I'm sorry to hear that!) | A question or an offer |

Never open a hobby talk with a phone greeting, and never close it with a formal letter closing.

### Daily load rules (these override any day entry)

1. At most 6 new patterns and 8 new cards a day. **Count patterns, not bullets or cards** (third review): a pattern is one sentence shape you can recall on its own, so a card that holds 2–3 sentences counts as 2–3 patterns. A pattern you have already mastered, or a simple swap of a detail in it, does not count as new. A day entry that hides more patterns than this inside one frame or card is trimmed or split (rule 9).
2. One grammar point a day, stated in one sentence.
3. Review stops at 8 minutes, finished or not.
4. Hear each new line before saying it.
5. One speaking task and one typed task. A book task replaces the day's own prompt.
6. A day is 60 minutes. If a block is added, another is removed.
7. A day is done when a changed version of the task works, not when a list is recited fast.
8. Mark every day and task Green, Amber or Red (below). Only Red repeats the skill tomorrow, with new details; Amber moves on.
9. If a day entry holds more than rule 1 allows, split it into day a and day b. Day b uses the same tasks with new details. The calendar slips, and that is intended.

**The progress rule: Green, Amber, Red** (second review, 16 November 2026; this is the one definition, and every "done when", exit test and mock in this plan uses it) [Plan's own]:

| Mark | When | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Green** | You understood the task and gave all the required points on your own. You read the model only to check afterwards. | Move on. |
| **Amber** | Understandable, but you hesitated or made a recurring mistake. | Move on with revision: put the top 1–2 mistakes on the error list (3.6) and revisit them inside later days. Do **not** repeat the day. |
| **Red** | You misunderstood the question, could not form an answer, or needed to read the model to answer. | Repeat the skill tomorrow with new details. |

- **Counts are targets, never gates.** Numbers of errors, word counts, speaking seconds, "N of M correct" and recitation speed are things to aim at and to record (6.1). They do not decide whether you move on.
- **Spelling and capital letters** never make a task Amber or Red if the message is clear.
- **Borderline cases** (third review):
  - A **forgotten required point** (contact details, an amount) in ordinary practice is **Amber**, unless the message cannot be used without it; then it is Red.
  - **Small grammar slips, or a wrong tense the listener still understands** (*I går ringer jag till banken.*, the present after *i går* or *förra helgen*), are Amber or Green, never Red on their own.
  - **Red** is kept for a misunderstood question, no answer, or needing the model.
  - The booking gate (4.7) keeps its stricter rule: every required point in every task. **[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**
- **Who marks it.** Day to day, you mark it yourself, honestly. The teacher's weekly rating (3.5) can change your mark.
- **Phase exit tests** pass when at most 1 task is Red and none of the Reds is a misunderstood question on a required point. Reds are repeated with new details within the next days, then the phase moves on.
- **Mocks** record Green, Amber or Red per subtest, plus the booking-gate checks (6.3, 6.4).
- **The one exception is the booking gate** (4.7). It stays a fixed test: two mocks in a row with every required point covered, finished in time, and an outside (teacher) rating of "understandable with some errors" or better; for listening or reading, about 70% on unseen questions. The engine-error count is tracked there, not gated.

**The honest cost.** Days 1–14 were rewritten to fit the load rules, and Day 3 is split into 3a and 3b, so Phase 1 is about 15 study days; it is longer only if a Red means repeating a day. Rule 9 stays as the fallback if a later day proves too heavy. The 84 days are a count of units, not dates.

### What is known about the exam

| Known | Tag |
|---|---|
| Four subtests (listening, speaking, reading, writing), each graded separately. Level 3 is the pass grade. There is no overall grade, and no subtest makes up for another. | [Official] |
| For citizenship you need level 3 or 4 in one of three pairs: **speaking + writing**, **listening + writing**, or **reading + speaking**. | [Official] |
| Migri, and OPH's own citizenship page, both say that two separate certificates can together make an accepted pair. One sentence on that OPH page still says the whole test must be done on one test day. Confirm with Migri at booking time. | [Official], one sentence in conflict |
| Every task and instruction is in Swedish only. | [Official] |
| The test day lasts about 5 hours including breaks. Spring 2027 Swedish tests are digital, on a test-site computer. | [Official] |
| Registration is binding. A refund is possible only for your own illness, with a medical certificate, and only if you cancel by 08:00 on the test morning. | [Official] |
| Level 3 tolerates a clear foreign accent, slow speech with some pauses, awkward grammar in demanding situations and limited, repetitive linking, as long as the message gets across. | [Official] |
| What blocks level 3: only routine one-line exchanges, frequent hesitation, relying on the other speaker, basic structures often wrong, fragmentary writing. A blank or unfinished task is the only error the sources treat as fatal. | [Official] |
| **Speaking sample tasks:** 1 minute to prepare plus 1.5 minutes about a person important to you; a phone call from a buyer answering your "for sale" ad (turns of about 10–25 seconds); a phone call to a repair company about something still broken (6 turns of 10–25 seconds); a 20-second voicemail saying you will be late. The other voice is a recording, and you cannot ask it to repeat. | [Official sample] |
| **Writing sample tasks:** an informal e-mail to a friend about an event (what, when, where, plus two more details; open and close properly); a letter to the editor giving your opinion with **at least three reasons**; a formal complaint about a bill (**which bill, at least two reasons, a suitable amount, contact details**). | [Official sample] |
| **Listening and reading:** multiple choice, true/false and short open answers. In the reading sample, wrong answers are not penalised, so answer everything. | [Official sample] |
| **Nine topic areas:** me and my background; home and housing; shops and services; culture; travel; health and wellbeing; work; environment; society. | [Official] |

| Unknown | Tag |
|---|---|
| Pass marks, marks per item, the time for each subtest, writing word counts, how long you must speak. | [Unknown] |
| Whether memorised or template-heavy answers are penalised. | [Unknown] |
| Whether the writing is typed in the digital test; headsets, timers, and whether you can restart an answer. | [Unknown] |
| How many times listening audio is played. Which Swedish accent the listening uses (one test-taker in 2022 said Finland-Swedish). | [Unknown] |
| Autumn 2027 test dates. | [Unknown] |

### What is decided and what is open

**Decided:**
- The core track is **speaking + writing**, because one sentence bank serves both.
- Listening and reading get a light daily minimum, so the pairs listening + writing and reading + speaking stay open.
- The day is 60–90 minutes, with rules for scaling it to 30 or 120.
- The core and the library, fresh mock prompts, and where the core lives: see the Decisions box at the top (16 November 2026).

**Open:**
- **The exam date and the pair.** You choose them at booking time, from mock evidence (section 4.7).
- **Combining partial-day certificates.** Migri and OPH's citizenship page both say it works; one OPH sentence still says "same test day". Confirm at booking time (section 8).
- **Your real starting level.** Day 0 measures it.
- **Your daily study time.**
- **Teacher availability.**

### An honest note on time

Going from nothing to B1 takes roughly **350 to 960 hours**. That range is a research estimate taken from two general sources (Cambridge English and the US State Department), not a measured Swedish YKI figure.

The 84-day core of this plan, at 60–90 minutes a day, gives about **84 to 126 hours**. You are not starting from nothing: you have had about 51 evening lessons, but your level is unknown. So the 84 days are a **core cycle**, not a promise. Since 16 November 2026 they are also a default order, not dates: you move on by the load rules above, so Phase 1 alone may take about 15 study days (14, plus the Day 3 split) and more if Reds need repeating. If the booking gate is not met after Day 84, you repeat Phase 4 with new prompts (section 4.6).

Test-takers who passed describe months of work, regular speaking practice, feedback and listening practice. **Nobody supports "templates alone".**

---

sections.title: 2. What we will learn, in priority order
sections.markdown:
The order follows one question: what is most likely to cost you level 3 if it is missing?

### 2.0 The core frames: the only lines you memorise (about 60)

**Section 2 is now the reference library** (Decisions, 16 November 2026). You memorise only this list, the 12 reason pairs and the 10 reactions named in section 1, and the 8 rescue phrases in 2.8. The rest of section 2 (templates T1–T16, the other reasons and reactions, the word lists) is looked up when a task needs it. T-numbers stay as aliases, so the book map and the curriculum still work. Every line below is already in the bank, where it has its English; `YKI-CORE-SHEET.md` lists them all with English. Three lines are adjusted: *Jag har tappat bort …* replaces *Jag vill anmäla att min plånbok är borta* for lost property, and the two seller lines each join two bank lines with *och* or *men*.

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

- **Me (6):** *Jag heter [___].* / *Jag kommer från [___].* / *Jag bor i [___].* / *Jag talar [___].* / *Jag lär mig svenska.* / *Jag jobbar som [___].*
- **Phone frame (4):** *Hej, det här är [namn].* / *Jag ringer angående [___].* / *Okej, då säger vi [torsdag klockan tio].* / *Tack för hjälpen. Hej då!*
- **Letter frame (5):** *Hej [namn]!* / *Hälsningar, [namn]* / *Jag skriver om [___].* / *Ni når mig på [telefonnummer] eller [e-postadress].* / *Med vänliga hälsningar, [namn]*
- **Ask (6):** *Jag skulle vilja [boka en tid].* / *Har ni en ledig tid [på tisdag]?* / *Passar det [på torsdag klockan tio]?* / *Hur mycket kostar [besöket]?* / *Jag undrar om [det finns lediga platser].* / *När kan jag [komma]?*

### 2.1 Task types and functions (priority 1)

**Why this comes first:** OPH's only preparation advice found is to "get to know the types of questions used in the test" [Official]. A task type is the exam's format, for example a phone dialogue. A function is what you do in it, for example complain or ask for something.

**Speaking task types in the practice material:**

| Type | What you do | Timing to practise |
|---|---|---|
| **Berätta** (tell) | Prepare, then talk alone about a person, an experience or a topic. | 1 min prep + 1.5 min talk [Official sample]. A class teacher gives 1 + 1 min [Teacher, unofficial]. Practise 1 + 1.5. |
| **Dialoger** (phone dialogues) | You read a short situation card, then answer a recorded voice turn by turn. | Turns of 10–25 s [Official sample]. About 15 s to read the card [Teacher, unofficial]. |
| **Reagera** (react) | A short spoken reaction to one situation. | 20 s prep + 25 s speaking [Teacher, unofficial]. |
| **Voicemail** | A short message, for example "I'll be late". | 20 s [Official sample]. |
| **Din åsikt** (your opinion) | Agree or disagree with a statement, with reasons. | 1 min prep + 1.5 min [Teacher, unofficial]. |

**Answer length** (third review) [Plan's own]: practise at a pace of about 80 words a minute. A 20-second turn then holds about 25–33 words, a 25-second turn about 33–40, 1 minute about 80 and 1.5 minutes about 120. **Writing task types:** an informal message, a formal message (request or complaint), and an opinion text [Official sample]. A class teacher gives 50–80 words for the informal and formal texts and 100–150 words for the opinion text [Teacher, unofficial]. **No official word count exists.**

### 2.2 The five-step opinion answer (priority 2)

**Why:** opinion tasks appear in speaking (Din åsikt) and writing (the letter to the editor, at least three reasons [Official sample]). One structure serves both.

| Step | What to say | Swedish frame |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Opinion | Your view, in the first sentence | *Jag tycker att …* / *Jag håller med.* / *Jag håller inte med.* |
| 2. Reason 1 + example | The strongest reason, then a concrete example | *För det första …* *Till exempel …* |
| 3. Reason 2 (and reason 3 in writing) | The next reason(s) | *För det andra …* *För det tredje …* |
| 4. Other view | One disadvantage or opposite opinion | *Å andra sidan …* / *En nackdel är att …* |
| 5. Conclusion | Repeat your view, linked to the reasons | *Men för mig är fördelarna större än nackdelarna. Därför tycker jag att …* |

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

**The trap:**
- After *För det första*, *Till exempel*, *Å andra sidan* and *Därför*, the **verb comes next**, then the subject: *För det första **sparar man** tid.*
- Never write *För det första man sparar tid.*
- Step 5 must agree with step 1. If you weighed both sides, say so in step 1 (*Jag tycker att det är bäst att göra båda*).
- **Speaking:** use at least 2 reasons. **Writing:** use at least 3.
- **Develop each reason** with an example and a link word; a ticked step is the minimum, not the finish (2.8, third review).

### 2.3 Templates per function: T1–T16, frames with slots (priority 3; reference library)

**Why:**
- Reusable openings, closings, connectors and skeletons with blank slots are the safe kind of memorising. Whole prepared answers are risky, because a memorised answer that misses the task's points scores low.
- No official rule on memorised answers exists [Unknown]. Evidence for slot templates is weak: one test-taker's account, plausible, nothing official.
- **Rule:** fill every slot with the prompt's own details, and delete any line the prompt does not ask for.

Square brackets [ ] are slots. T17–T20 are in `YKI-NEW-TEMPLATES-T17-T20.md`.
