| 40–100 | **Writing set:** W1 15 min, W2 25 min, W3 20 min [Plan's own limits]. Typed, with no spelling help. |
| 100–105 | Break. |
| 105–125 | **Listening and reading:** 2 easy-news clips (3 facts and all numbers each) and 2 notices (5 questions each), scored against the text. |
| 125–145 | **Check your results** (section 6): mark each subtest Green, Amber or Red, tick the booking-gate points (every required point, every task in time), count the targets, and prepare the teacher pack: every recording and text. |

**Speaking set (seen practice):**
- **S1, person/experience** (1 + 1.5 min): *Berätta om en resa som du minns.*
- **S2, seller call** (6 turns, 20 s):
  - Card: *Du säljer en soffa. En köpare ringer. Svara på frågorna. Föreslå en tid och säg var du bor.*
  - The other voice: 1. *Hej, jag ringer om soffan. Finns den kvar?* 2. *Hur gammal är den?* 3. *Vilken färg har den?* 4. *Vad kostar den?* 5. *Kan jag få den för 80 euro?* 6. *När kan jag komma och hämta den?*
- **S3, complaint call** (6 turns, 20 s):
  - Card: *Du har köpt ett par vinterskor. Efter en vecka gick de sönder. Ring butiken. Förklara problemet och säg vad du vill.*
  - The other voice: 1. *Skobutiken, hej.* 2. *Vad gäller det?* 3. *När köpte du dem?* 4. *Har du kvittot kvar?* 5. *Vi kan skicka dem på reparation.* 6. *Okej, kom till butiken med skorna och kvittot.*
- **S4, voicemail** (20 s): *Du har en tid hos läkaren i morgon klockan tio, men du kan inte komma. Lämna ett meddelande.*
- **S5, three reactions** (20 s + 25 s each): a) *Din kollega berättar att hon ska gifta sig.* b) *Din vän har brutit benet.* c) *Din granne frågar om han kan låna din bil på lördag, men du behöver den själv.*
- **S6, opinion** (1 + 1.5 min): *Påstående: Alla borde lära sig laga mat i skolan. Håller du med? Motivera din åsikt.*

**Writing set (seen practice):**

| Task | Prompt | Required points |
|---|---|---|
| **W1, informal** | *Din vän ska besöka dig i Helsingfors. Föreslå en dag och en aktivitet, skriv var ni kan träffas och fråga vad din vän vill äta.* | 6: opening, day, activity, meeting place, food question, closing. |
| **W2, letter to the editor** | *Skriv en insändare: Alla borde åka kollektivt i stället för med bil. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.* | 8: topic line, opinion, reason 1, reason 2, reason 3, an example, other view, matching conclusion. |
| **W3, formal** | *Du har köpt en vattenkokare i en webbutik. Den är trasig. Skriv till butiken. Skriv när du köpte den, vad som är fel, vad du vill att butiken gör och ge dina kontaktuppgifter.* | 6: when bought (with order number), what is wrong, what you want, contact details, formal opening, formal closing. |

**Models (seen practice).**

W2:
> *Jag vill skriva om bilar i staden. Jag tycker att fler människor borde åka buss och tåg i stället för bil. För det första är det bättre för miljön. Bussar och tåg ger mindre utsläpp per person. För det andra sparar man pengar. Det kostar mycket att ha bil, till exempel bensin, försäkring och parkering. För det tredje blir det mindre trafik i centrum, och då blir luften renare. Å andra sidan är kollektivtrafiken inte bra överallt. På landet går bussen kanske bara två gånger om dagen. Men i staden är fördelarna större än nackdelarna. Därför tycker jag att man ska åka kollektivt när det är möjligt. Alex Kumar, Esbo*

S4:
> *Hej, det här är Alex Kumar. Jag har en tid i morgon klockan tio, men tyvärr kan jag inte komma. Kan jag få en ny tid nästa vecka? Ring mig gärna. Tack!* (about 30 words, which fits 20 seconds at a careful pace)

**Common errors on mock days:**

| Error | Fix |
|---|---|
| Only two reasons in W2 | The official sample asks for at least three. |
| No contact details or order number in W3 | Both are required points. |
| *För det tredje det blir …* | *För det tredje blir det …* |
| *Jag vet inte vad är fel.* | *Jag vet inte vad som är fel.* (In an indirect question, *vad* as the subject needs *som*.) |
| A voicemail over 20 seconds | Cut the reason to one short clause. |
| Stopping a call turn early because you missed the voice | Use one of the three recovery options: answer it if you understood it; answer the part you understood; or give the card's next piece of information without agreeing to anything (*Jag kan komma på fredag efter klockan fyra.*). Never say *Okej* by reflex. [Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it] |

**Pass rules:** section 6.

---

sections.title: 6. The weekly rhythm and the four-weekly mock
sections.markdown:
### 6.1 The weekly rhythm

**Days 1–6 of each week: study days**, 60–90 minutes in the format of 3.1.

- **On the first study day of the week,** start with the top-3 error drill (3.6), taking 5 minutes from the "New" block.
- **On one study day,** send the teacher pack: the 2 newest recordings, the 2 newest texts, and the task cards with their required points.

**Day 7 of each week: light day**, 30–40 minutes:
- Your due cards.
- One task re-recorded from memory with a new detail.
- One listening item.

**Every week, write down:**
- Your Green, Amber and Red marks for the week's days and tasks (section 1), and which skills were Red.
- The targets: the share of required points you covered, how many tasks you finished in time, engine errors per written text, and your listening and reading scores.
- The teacher's A–D ratings.

This is your progress record. The Green, Amber, Red marks decide whether you move on; the numbers are targets that show the trend, not gates.

### 6.2 The four-weekly mock (Days 28, 56 and 84; weekly after Day 84)

**Speaking set** (about 25–30 minutes, back to back, recorded):

| Task | Format | Timing | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Person or experience | 1 min prep + 1.5 min | [Official sample] |
| S2 | Phone call: seller in one mock, buyer in the next | 6 turns of 20 s | [Plan's practice limit, inside the 10–25 s sample range] |
| S3 | Complaint or repair call | 6 turns of 20 s | [same] |
| S4 | Voicemail | 20 s | [Official sample] |
| S5 | Three reactions | 20 s prep + 25 s each | [Teacher, unofficial] |
| S6 | Opinion | 1 min prep + 1.5 min | [Teacher, unofficial] |

**Writing set** (60 minutes, typed, no spelling help; the time limits are [Plan's own]):

| Task | Format | Time | Length target |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Informal message (event, visit or invitation) | 15 min | about 50–80 words [Teacher, unofficial] |
| W2 | Letter to the editor, at least three reasons | 25 min | about 100–150 words [Teacher, unofficial] |
| W3 | Formal message: a complaint with all four official-sample points, or a request with contact details. In a mock that counts towards booking, W3 is a formal complaint (the mock recipe in the teacher-only reserve file). | 20 min | about 50–80 words [Teacher, unofficial] |

**Listening and reading** (20 minutes):
- 2 unseen easy-news clips, each with 3 facts and all its numbers.
- 2 unseen notices, each with 5 questions.
- Score each against the text.
- **For a mock that will count towards booking a listening or reading day,** the teacher or a helper must write about 8 unseen questions per clip or text, in the exam's three formats: multiple choice, true/false and short open answers. Only those scores count for the 70% rule.

**Mock 1 (Day 28) is short,** because Phase 2 is only half done: S2, S4, S5, W1 and W3, plus 1 clip and 1 notice.

**The fresh-prompt rule** (decided 16 November 2026):
- **Every prompt printed in this plan, the curriculum and the appendix is seen practice.** You have read it, and these files have been pasted into an AI chat, so moving text cannot make it unseen.
- **The previously printed mock prompts are seen practice too** (third review). Until the second review the learner's book map printed a short description of each of the 40 held-back book tasks, and the book itself is the learner's. So the held-back tasks can no longer be treated as unseen.
- **Mocks that count towards booking** (Mock 3 and every later mock) use prompts you have never seen, from one of two sources, in this order: (1) the teacher writes them; (2) only as a fallback, an AI writes them on the day and the helper reads them out (the helper, not the learner, sees the chat). A printed prompt and a held-back book task are never used in a counted mock.
- **The reserve stays teacher-only.** The 40 held-back tasks, the balanced mock recipe and the gap table are in `teacher-only/YKI-MOCK-RESERVE.md`, for the teacher or the helper; the learner does not open it. The recipe still defines every counted mock; the held-back tasks now serve Mocks 1 and 2 and spare practice.
- **Every counted mock is balanced** (the recipe): one talk, one seller or buyer call, one repair or complaint call, one voicemail, three reactions, one opinion talk, one informal message, one letter with at least three reasons, and one formal complaint.
- **Mocks 1 and 2 and the phase exit tests** may reuse printed prompts if a helper changes the details (names, places, times, the problem). Mocks 1 and 2 may also use any held-back task (since the third review nothing needs to be kept back for the counted mocks).
- New easy-news clips and notices are unseen by nature; the listening and reading questions for a counting mock are written by the teacher or a helper.

### 6.3 How a mock is checked: the teacher first, then you

1. **The teacher** rates every speaking and writing task on the 3.5 sheet: points covered, a rating from A to D, the top 3 errors, and Green, Amber or Red.
2. **You** then check and record:
   - **the booking-gate checks:** required points covered, task by task; time: no turn cut off, no writing task over its limit;
   - **the targets** (tracked, not gated): word counts; engine errors per text (G1, G2, G3, G5); the listening and reading score as a percentage;
   - **Green, Amber or Red per subtest** (section 1).
3. **Where your count and the teacher's disagree, the teacher's count stands.**

**The early skill signal (Mocks 1 and 2).** Fill in this small table after each of the first two mocks. It shows which pair is getting stronger; it decides nothing. The pair, the date and the sitting are chosen only at booking time (4.7).

| Subtest | Mock 1 (G / A / R) | Mock 2 (G / A / R) |
|---|---|---|
| Speaking | | |
| Writing | | |
| Listening | | |
| Reading | | |

### 6.4 What counts as a pass [Plan's own rules]

| Item | Pass |
|---|---|
| Required points | Every point in every speaking and writing task |
| Time | Every task inside its limit |
| Written accuracy | Count the engine errors per text and track the number. It is not a pass rule: a 150-word letter and a 50-word message cannot share one limit. |
| Teacher rating | A or B on every task |
| Listening and reading | About 70% or more on unseen, teacher- or helper-written questions in the three formats (6.2). This is the research's own benchmark, not official, and it matters only for a pair with listening or reading. |

- **This table is the booking gate** (4.7). It is the one fixed test in the plan; everywhere else you move on by Green, Amber or Red (section 1).
- **Every mock also records Green, Amber or Red per subtest** (6.3).
- **Mocks 1 and 2 are progress checks.** They do not gate a phase; the phase exit tests do that. Their Green, Amber and Red marks per subtest are the early skill signal (6.3), not a decision.
- **Mock 3 and every later mock count towards the booking gate:** two passes in a row (4.7).

---

sections.title: 7. The listening and reading minimum
sections.markdown:
**How much** (third review, 16 November 2026): block 5 of the daily format (3.1). **A 60-minute day has 8 minutes** (minutes 48–56): the routine in 7.3 or 7.4, shortened to 8 minutes. **A 90-minute day has 10 minutes** (minutes 72–82): the full routine. Light days do one item; mock and exit-test days set their own amount, and their entry says how much.

### 7.1 Why it matters

- **It keeps two pairs open:** listening + writing, and reading + speaking.
- **Speaking needs it too.** In the phone tasks you must understand a recorded voice that you cannot ask to repeat.
- **Strategy helps, but it does not replace comprehension.** Listening and reading cannot be templated the way speaking and writing can, and they need real comprehension. Strategy still helps you use the Swedish you have: search for the information the question asks for; expect synonyms (the question rarely uses the text's own words); watch negatives and changes; catch numbers, dates and prices; and notice whether someone accepts, refuses, cancels or changes a plan (7.5). *(Corrected 16 November 2026, second review: an earlier version said tricks work only for speaking and writing.)* [Plan's own coaching, not an official claim]
- **It gives cheap points.** Numbers, dates and the meaning-flip words are the cheapest points you can earn.

### 7.2 What to use

- **Yle's easy-Swedish news, "Nyheter på lätt svenska".** It is Finland-Swedish, with sound and text. Use a **new** item every listening day.
- **Real Finland-Swedish notices:**
  - the Swedish side of bilingual signs, leaflets, timetables and shop notices;
  - notices from a housing company;
  - letters from health services or the city.
- **Short texts the teacher hands out.**
- **Which accent the exam uses is unknown** [Unknown]. Practising with Finland-Swedish is this plan's choice, not an exam fact.

### 7.3 The 10-minute listening routine (4 days a week)

| Minutes | What you do |
|---|---|
| 0–1 | Read only the headline. Guess 3 words you expect to hear. |
| 1–4 | Listen **once** without the text. Write 3 facts: who, what, where. Do not stop at unknown words. |
| 4–6 | Listen again. Write every number, date, time, name and place. |
| 6–8 | Read the text. Check your facts and numbers. Underline 3 things you missed. |
| 8–10 | Read 3 sentences from the text aloud. Make 2 cards: one word, one number or date phrase. |

### 7.4 The 10-minute reading routine (2 days a week)

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

| Minutes | What you do |
|---|---|
| 0–1 | What kind of text is it (an ad, a notice, a letter, news), and what is it about? Take 20 seconds. |
| 1–4 | Answer the 5 notice questions: **what, when, where, for whom, cost or condition.** |
| 4–6 | Find any meaning-flip words (2.6). Does one change the meaning (*inte, stängt, inställt, i stället*)? |
| 6–8 | Write 3 true/false statements about the text, one of them false, and answer them the next day. |
| 8–10 | Make 2 cards. Note one pair of words with the same meaning (for example *billig / prisvärd*); questions often use a different word from the text. |

### 7.5 Exam habits to practise in every item

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

- **Read the question first.** Know which question word you need (*vem, vad, var, när, hur många, varför*), and what kind of answer it wants (the question-to-answer reflex, 2.6).
- **Search for the asked information,** not for every word. Find the place in the text or the recording where the question's topic comes up.
- **Expect synonyms.** The question often uses another word than the text: *billig / prisvärd*, *ringa / kontakta*, *gratis / utan kostnad*.
- **Watch negatives and changes:** *inte, aldrig, ingen, men, i stället, tyvärr, inställt, flyttat, ändrat*. They often turn the first thing you heard around.
- **Catch numbers, dates and prices,** and what each number counts.
- **Notice the decision:** does the speaker accept, refuse, cancel or change something? Many questions ask exactly that.
- **Strategy does not replace comprehension.** It helps you use the Swedish you have; it cannot add Swedish you lack.
- **Answer every item.** In the reading sample, wrong answers are not penalised [Official sample].
- **For an open answer,** write 1–4 words you heard or read.
- **Don't translate the whole text.** Find the keyword and read only the sentence around it.
- **If you're stuck, move on** and come back at the end.
- **Once a month,** work out your facts-right and numbers-right percentages, and enter them in the progress record.

---

sections.title: 8. Honest limits, open questions, and the pre-registration checklist
sections.markdown:
### 8.1 What this plan cannot do

1. **It cannot guarantee level 3.** Only official raters give grades. The teacher's A–D rating is not an official grade either.
2. **It may not be enough time.** From nothing, B1 takes roughly 350–960 hours (an estimate, not a YKI measurement). The 84-day core gives about 84–126 hours. Your starting level is unknown, so the core may need repeating.
3. **The templates will not cover every task.** In one practice book, about 14% of speaking tasks and 8 of 21 writing tasks fall outside the top five functions [Book count]. Twenty templates, grouped into six engines, reduce this gap; they do not remove it. Real tasks may differ again.
4. **Its Swedish is unreviewed.** The plan cannot check itself. A teacher must.
5. **It cannot copy the digital test.** The screens, typing rules, headsets and timers are unknown.
6. **The listening accent is unknown.** Read-aloud practice is weaker than real audio.
7. **Self-checks miss your own repeated errors.** That is why the teacher's weekly rating can change your Green, Amber or Red marks, and why the booking gate needs an outside rating.
8. **Writing may be the hard part.** One old study (2015) found writing to be the weakest subtest in that year's group. It is old and covers one group.
9. **Published results are not a pass rate.** One table of Swedish intermediate results (2020–2024) shows the share at level 3 or above falling from about 63% to 46%. The table does not define its terms, so it is **not** a pass rate. It is still a reason not to rely on templates alone.
10. **The certificate is not the whole test of your Swedish.** Migri also compares your real language use when you deal with them [Official]. A minimum certificate does not remove the need for usable Swedish.
11. **The citizenship rules are changing.** New rules start on 1 January 2027, and applications received from 1 March 2027 follow them. They add a separate citizenship (society) test. The language requirement appears to continue, but the law text was not checked.

### 8.2 Questions to ask

**Migri:**
1. Can a certificate from a writing + listening day and one from a speaking + reading day be combined into a speaking + writing pair for citizenship? (Migri's YKI page and OPH's citizenship page both say two certificates can be combined; one sentence on the OPH page still says the whole test must be done on one test day.)
2. For applications received from 1 March 2027, is the YKI language requirement unchanged: level 3 or 4 in one of the three pairs?

**OPH or the test centre:**

3. Is writing typed in the digital Swedish test? Which keyboard is used, and how are *å, ä, ö* typed?
4. Is there a digital practice test for **Swedish**? The one found was for Finnish.
5. In speaking: is the task card shown on screen? Is there an on-screen timer? Can you restart an answer?
6. In listening: how many times is each recording played? Can you read the questions before the audio?
7. How long does each subtest take?
8. Which Helsinki-area centres hold the Swedish intermediate test on your chosen date?
9. How do you request special arrangements (for example for noise)? They must be requested at registration.
10. What are the autumn 2027 dates and the 2027 fees?

**The teacher:**

11. Please check every Swedish line in this plan, starting with the banks in section 2.
12. Which Finland-Swedish words should I prefer? These candidates come from memory and are **unverified**:
    - *räkning* for a bill;
    - *inhiberad* for cancelled;
    - *husbolag* for a housing company;
    - *disponent* for a housing manager;
    - *FPA* for the social insurance office.
13. Are the timings and word counts in this plan still what current practice uses? These are the 20 + 25 s reactions, the 1 + 1.5 min opinion, and the 50–80 and 100–150 words.
14. Is my speaking and writing "understandable with some errors"?
15. **Teacher to confirm: *uppge* or *ange* versus *ge dina kontaktuppgifter*.** About 14 practice prompts say *ge dina kontaktuppgifter*. A real task card may say *uppge* or *ange* (since the third review *ange* is one of the 23 instruction words in 2.6). The prompts stay as they are until you answer.
16. Other lines to confirm: is the present with *sedan* also right (*Det läcker vatten sedan i lördags*), or only the perfect? Is *avskedsfika* natural in Finland? *Säg till senast onsdag* or *senast på onsdag*? *i bussen* or *på bussen*? *ska ha en viktig intervju* or *ska på en viktig intervju*?

### 8.3 Checklist before you register

- [ ] The booking gate in 4.7 is met: two recent mocks in a row, rated by the teacher.
- [ ] The pair is chosen with the table in 4.7.
- [ ] If you are combining partial-day certificates, you have confirmed with Migri at booking time that it works (a written answer is safest).
- [ ] The date, window, centre and fee are confirmed on the official YKI registration service. Some official pages have shown different dates.
- [ ] You know the window opens at 10:00 on its first day, the payment link is valid for 1–3 days, and registration counts only once you have paid.
- [ ] You have valid original photo ID: a passport, ID card or residence permit card. A driving licence does not count, and nor does a photo of an ID.
- [ ] You can attend for about 5 hours. Latecomers cannot sit the test.
- [ ] Any special arrangements were requested at registration.
- [ ] You accept the refund rule: registration is binding, and a refund is possible only for your own illness, with a medical certificate, cancelling by 08:00 on the test morning and applying within two weeks.
- [ ] You know the day rules:
  - phones, watches and all electronic devices are collected, even for breaks;
  - no dictionaries or study material;
  - a pencil and eraser are provided;
  - food is allowed for the breaks.
- [ ] Phase 5 (the taper) is planned for the 7 days before the test.
- [ ] You know results take about two months, and that a re-rating rarely changes a grade (in 2025, 128 requests and 7 changed grades) [Official]. Prepare to pass the first time.

---

sections.title: Appendix: practice prompts, 10 per function (seen practice)
sections.markdown:
**How to use these prompts:**
- These are **seen practice**: they are printed in your own plan. Use them for daily practice, spare tasks and the phase exit tests (with a helper changing the details). They never serve as a mock that counts towards booking (6.2, fresh-prompt rule).
- **S** marks a speaking prompt and **W** a writing prompt.
- Use the timings in section 6.2. Phone prompts have 6 turns. If no helper can play the other voice, write 6 short questions for the other side first, then cover them.
- **"Points"** are the required points. They are this plan's own, modelled on the official sample task types.
- Every written task to a company or office also needs a formal opening, a formal closing and your contact details.

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

### A. Request, booking, asking for information

**Default points:** who you are; what you want; when; at least one question; a polite close. In writing, also contact details.

| # | Type | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | S | *Ring en frisör och boka en tid.* | Suggest 2 possible times; ask the price; confirm the time. |
| A2 | W | *Skriv till ett gym. Fråga vad ett medlemskap kostar, när gymmet är öppet och om man kan prova en gång gratis.* | All 3 questions. |
| A3 | S | *Ring biblioteket. Du vill förlänga lånet av en bok.* | Which book; why; for how long; ask about a fee. |
| A4 | W | *Skriv till din chef. Du vill ha ledigt en dag nästa månad. Förklara varför och föreslå en dag.* | Reason; date; offer a solution for the work. |
| A5 | S | *Ring läkarmottagningen och boka en tid. Du har haft feber i tre dagar.* | Symptoms and how long; when you can come; repeat the time. |
| A6 | W | *Skriv till en hyresvärd. Du har sett en annons om en lägenhet. Fråga hur stor den är, när man kan flytta in och om du kan se lägenheten.* | Which ad; all 3 questions; when you can come to view it. |
| A7 | S | *Ring en taxifirma och beställ en taxi till flygplatsen i morgon bitti.* | Address; time; number of people and bags; ask the price. |
| A8 | W | *Skriv till skolan där ditt barn går. Du vill veta när föräldramötet är och om det finns information på engelska.* | Who you are (whose parent); both questions. |
| A9 | S | *Du är i en butik. Be personalen om hjälp. Du letar efter en present till en vän.* | For whom; how much you want to spend; one question; thanks. |
| A10 | W | *Skriv till en restaurang. Du vill boka ett bord för åtta personer på lördag. Fråga om de har vegetarisk mat.* | Day, time, number of people; the vegetarian question. |

### B. Buying and selling by phone (both roles)

**Default points.** As the seller: the item is still available; its age; its condition; the price; an answer to a lower offer; a time and your address. As the buyer: who you are; which ad; 3 questions; an offer; a time to come and look.

| # | Type | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | S, seller | *Du säljer en barnvagn. En köpare ringer. Svara på frågorna och föreslå en tid.* | — |
| B2 | S, buyer | *Du har sett en annons om en begagnad tv. Ring säljaren. Fråga om skick, ålder och pris, och försök få ett lägre pris.* | — |
| B3 | S, seller | *Du säljer ett bord och fyra stolar. En köpare ringer och vill veta mer.* | Size and colour. |
| B4 | S, buyer | *Ring om en cykel i en annons. Du vill veta om den passar en vuxen och när du kan provcykla.* | The size question; a test-ride time. |
| B5 | W, seller | *Skriv en annons. Du säljer din soffa. Skriv vad den kostar, hur gammal den är och hur man kontaktar dig.* | Condition; where to collect it. |
| B6 | S, seller | *Du säljer en vinterjacka. En köpare ringer och frågar om storlek och färg.* | Size; colour; where to meet. |
| B7 | S, buyer | *Ring om en begagnad dator. Fråga hur gammal den är, om batteriet är bra och om du kan betala med mobilen.* | All 3 questions. |
| B8 | W, buyer | *Skriv ett meddelande till en säljare. Du vill köpa en bokhylla från en annons. Ställ två frågor och föreslå en tid när du kan hämta den.* | Which ad; 2 questions; a pick-up time. |
| B9 | S, seller | *Du säljer dina gamla skidor. Köparen vill betala mindre. Förhandla om priset.* | A counter-offer; agree on a price. |
| B10 | S, buyer | *Ring om en lägenhet som hyrs ut. Fråga om hyran, om el ingår och när lägenheten är ledig.* | All 3 questions; a viewing time. |

### C. Complaint by phone (repair, service)

**Default points:** who you are; what it concerns; the problem; since when; a protest with a reason; what you want, and by when; a close.

| # | Type | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | S | *Din mobiltelefon har varit på reparation, men skärmen fungerar fortfarande inte. Ring butiken.* | When it was repaired. |
| C2 | S | *Du beställde en pizza för en timme sedan, men den har inte kommit. Ring restaurangen.* | What you ordered; food now or money back. |
| C3 | S | *Internet hemma har inte fungerat på tre dagar. Ring företaget.* | Your customer number; what it stops you doing; ask about compensation. |
| C4 | S | *En hantverkare skulle komma i dag klockan tio, men ingen har kommit. Ring firman.* | Your booking; a new time. |
| C5 | S | *Du har fått fel vara från en webbutik. Ring kundtjänst.* | Order number; what you ordered and what you got; ask who pays for the return. |
| C6 | S | *Din granne spelar hög musik varje natt. Ring hyresvärden.* | Your flat; how it affects you. |
| C7 | S | *Diskmaskinen läcker vatten, fast den är ny. Ring butiken där du köpte den.* | When you bought it; the guarantee. |
| C8 | S | *Hissen i ditt hus har varit trasig i en vecka. Ring hyresvärden.* | Why it is urgent for you. |
| C9 | S | *Kemtvätten har tappat bort din kostym. Ring dem.* | When you left it; your receipt. |
| C10 | S | *Du bodde på ett hotell. Rummet var smutsigt och duschen fungerade inte. Ring hotellet.* | Your dates; both problems; ask for part of the money back. |

### D. Written complaint (bill or product)

**Default points:**
- **For a bill** (from the official sample): which bill (number, date, amount); at least two reasons; a suitable amount; contact details.
- **For a product:** when you bought it (order or receipt); what is wrong; what you want; contact details.

| # | Type | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | W | *Du har fått en faktura från en städfirma på 320 euro, men de städade bara två timmar. Skriv till firman.* | — |
| D2 | W | *Ditt elbolag har skickat en faktura som är dubbelt så hög som vanligt. Skriv och klaga.* | Your normal amount. |
| D3 | W | *Du köpte en jacka på nätet. Efter två veckor gick dragkedjan sönder. Skriv till butiken.* | Product version. |
| D4 | W | *En flyttfirma har skadat ditt bord och tagit betalt för fler timmar än vad som var bestämt. Skriv till firman.* | The damage and the hours are your two reasons. |
| D5 | W | *Du har betalat en faktura, men du har fått en påminnelse med en avgift på 10 euro. Skriv till företaget.* | When you paid; ask them to remove the fee. |
| D6 | W | *Ditt gym har tagit betalt för en månad efter att du sa upp ditt medlemskap. Skriv och be om pengarna tillbaka.* | When you cancelled; the amount. |
| D7 | W | *Du köpte en vattenkokare för tre veckor sedan. Den har slutat fungera. Skriv till butiken.* | Product version; the guarantee. |
| D8 | W | *Du har fått en faktura från tandläkaren för en behandling som du inte har fått. Skriv och förklara.* | Two reasons; what you want. |
| D9 | W | *En webbutik skickade din beställning tre veckor för sent, men du betalade för expressfrakt. Skriv och klaga.* | The amount you want back. |
| D10 | W | *Du har hyrt en bil, och firman vill att du betalar för en skada som fanns där förut. Skriv till firman.* | Two reasons (for example a photo, a witness). |

### E. Reactions (Reagera: 20 s prep + 25 s, all speaking)

**Default points:** react in a way that fits the news; one relevant detail or question; an offer or a close.

| # | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | *Din vän berättar att hon har klarat körkortsprovet.* | Congratulate. |
| E2 | *Din kollega säger att hans pappa har dött.* | Condolence; offer support. |
| E3 | *En granne har hjälpt dig att bära möbler.* | Thank; offer something back. |
| E4 | *Din vän är sjuk och kan inte komma på din fest.* | Sympathy; a new plan. |
| E5 | *En kollega erbjuder dig skjuts hem, men du har cykeln med dig.* | Thank; refuse with a reason. |
| E6 | *Någon trampar på din fot i bussen och ber om ursäkt.* | Accept the apology. |
| E7 | *Din vän har fått en ny lägenhet.* | Congratulate; offer help with the move. |
| E8 | *Din granne frågar om du kan vattna hennes blommor nästa vecka. Du kan.* | Accept; ask when, and about the keys. |
| E9 | *Du har glömt din väns födelsedag. Ring och säg förlåt.* | Apologise; make up for it. |
| E10 | *Din kollega har jobbat mycket och ser trött ut.* | Show sympathy; offer help. |

### F. Apology, cancelling, being late

**Default points:** who you are; the apology; a short reason; what happens now (a new time or a solution).

| # | Type | Prompt | Extra points |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | S, voicemail | *Du kommer tjugo minuter för sent till en jobbintervju. Ring och lämna ett meddelande.* | Your new arrival time. |
| F2 | W | *Du kan inte komma på svenskkursen i morgon. Skriv till läraren.* | Ask about the homework. |
| F3 | S, voicemail | *Du måste avboka din tid hos frisören. Lämna ett meddelande och be om en ny tid.* | — |
| F4 | W | *Du glömde ett möte med din granne. Skriv och be om ursäkt.* | Suggest a new time. |
| F5 | S | *Du har lånat en bok av en vän och tappat bort den. Ring och berätta.* | Offer to buy a new one. |
| F6 | S, voicemail | *Tåget är försenat och du hinner inte till din väns middag i tid.* | Your new time; "start without me". |
| F7 | W | *Du måste avboka ett hotellrum. Skriv till hotellet.* | Booking details; ask about a refund. |
| F8 | W | *Du har råkat skada en annan bils backspegel på en parkering. Skriv en lapp till ägaren.* | Offer to pay; contact details. |
| F9 | S | *Du är sjuk och kan inte jobba i morgon. Ring din chef.* | How long you will be away; anything urgent. |
| F10 | W | *Du kan inte komma på din väns bröllop. Skriv ett kort och förklara.* | Congratulate; a wish. |

### G. Polite refusal

**Default points:** thanks or acknowledgement; a clear "no"; a reason; an alternative or a kind close.

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | S | *En kollega frågar om du kan jobba för henne på lördag. Du kan inte.* |
| G2 | W | *En förening frågar om du vill vara med i styrelsen. Tacka nej.* |
| G3 | S | *En säljare ringer och erbjuder dig ett nytt mobilabonnemang. Du vill inte ha det.* |
| G4 | W | *Din granne bjuder dig på grillfest, men du ska resa bort.* |
| G5 | S | *Din vän vill låna din bil i helgen, men du behöver den själv.* |
| G6 | S | *Din chef frågar om du kan stanna två timmar extra i kväll. Du har en tid hos läkaren.* |
| G7 | W | *En vän vill att du följer med på en resa till Lappland, men det är för dyrt för dig just nu.* |
| G8 | S | *En granne frågar om du kan ta hand om hennes hund i en vecka. Du är allergisk.* |
| G9 | W | *Ett företag erbjuder dig ett jobb, men du har redan tackat ja till ett annat. Tacka nej.* |
| G10 | S | *En kollega vill att du håller ett tal på festen. Du vill inte.* |

### H. Invitation and event message

**Default points, for an event** (from the official sample): what, when, where, plus two more details; an invitation question; an opening and a closing. **For an invitation:** what; when; where; a reply-by date.

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | W | *Skriv till en vän om en loppis i ditt område. Skriv vad, när och var, och ge två andra detaljer.* |
| H2 | S | *Ring din vän Sara och bjud in henne till middag hos dig på fredag.* (Also: ask about food the friend does not eat.) |
| H3 | W | *Bjud in dina kollegor till en avskedsfika. Skriv när, var och varför.* |
| H4 | W | *Skriv till en vän om en filmkväll på biblioteket. Skriv vad, när och var, och ge två andra detaljer.* |
| H5 | S | *Din vän ringer och bjuder in dig till en fest. Tacka ja och fråga om detaljer.* |
| H6 | W | *Bjud in dina grannar till en städdag på gården. Skriv när, vad man ska göra och vad som händer efteråt.* |
| H7 | W | *Skriv till en vän om ett språkkafé där man kan prata svenska. Skriv vad, när och var, och ge två andra detaljer.* |
| H8 | S | *Fråga en kollega om hon vill följa med på en promenad på lunchen.* |
| H9 | W | *Skriv en inbjudan till ditt barns födelsedagskalas.* |
| H10 | W | *Din vän har aldrig varit i Helsingfors. Skriv och föreslå vad ni kan göra en dag i sommar.* |

### I. Advice and suggestions

**Default points:** at least 2 pieces of advice; a reason or an example for each; a friendly close (writing: an opening and a closing).

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | S | *Din vän vill lära sig svenska. Ge två råd.* |
| I2 | W | *En vän ska flytta till Finland. Skriv och ge råd om boende och arbete.* |
| I3 | S | *Din kollega sover dåligt. Ge råd.* |
| I4 | W | *Din vän vill börja träna men har lite tid. Skriv och ge förslag.* |
| I5 | S | *En ny granne frågar var man kan handla billig mat. Ge tips.* |
| I6 | W | *En vän ska besöka Finland på vintern. Skriv vad din vän ska packa.* |
| I7 | S | *Din vän har problem med sin hyresvärd. Föreslå vad din vän kan göra.* |
| I8 | W | *En vän vill spara pengar. Skriv tre förslag.* |
| I9 | S | *En kollega ska hålla en presentation och är nervös. Ge råd.* |
| I10 | W | *Din vän vill skaffa en hund. Skriv vad din vän ska tänka på.* |

### J. Report to an authority, a landlord or lost property

**Default points:** who you are; what happened; when and where; a description; what you want; contact details.

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| J1 | S | *Du har tappat din plånbok på bussen. Ring hittegodset.* |
| J2 | W | *Det läcker vatten från taket i ditt badrum. Skriv till hyresvärden.* |
| J3 | S | *Någon har stulit din cykel. Ring polisen och anmäl stölden.* |
| J4 | W | *Du har flyttat. Skriv till din bank och meddela din nya adress.* (Also: from which date.) |
| J5 | S | *Gatlampan utanför ditt hus fungerar inte. Ring kommunen.* |
| J6 | W | *Din granne har lämnat sopor i trapphuset i flera dagar. Skriv till hyresvärden.* |
| J7 | S | *Du har glömt din jacka på ett tåg. Ring och fråga om någon har hittat den.* |
| J8 | W | *Ditt bankkort är borta. Skriv till banken och be dem spärra kortet.* |
| J9 | S | *En bil har stått parkerad framför din port i tre dagar. Ring hyresvärden.* |
| J10 | W | *Någon har skadat lekplatsen på gården. Skriv till hyresvärden.* (Also: why it is dangerous.) |

### K. Opinion

**Default points.**
- **Speaking:** a clear opinion; at least 2 reasons; an example; the other view; a conclusion that matches the opinion.
- **Writing** (a letter to the editor): also a topic line and **at least three reasons** [Official sample].

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | S | *Påstående: Det är bättre att jobba hemma än på kontoret. Håller du med?* |
| K2 | W | *Skriv en insändare: Alla barn borde ha en mobiltelefon. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.* |
| K3 | S | *Påstående: Man ska inte äta kött. Håller du med?* |
| K4 | W | *Skriv en insändare: Bussarna i staden borde vara gratis. Ge minst tre skäl.* |
| K5 | S | *Påstående: Det är bättre att resa med tåg än med flyg. Håller du med?* |
| K6 | W | *Skriv en insändare: Alla vuxna borde lära sig ett nytt språk. Ge minst tre skäl.* |
| K7 | S | *Påstående: Sociala medier gör mer skada än nytta. Håller du med?* |
| K8 | W | *Skriv en insändare: Det är bättre att bo i ett eget hus än i en lägenhet. Ge minst tre skäl.* |
| K9 | S | *Påstående: Alla borde ha ett husdjur. Håller du med?* |
| K10 | W | *Skriv en insändare: Skolan borde börja senare på morgonen. Ge minst tre skäl.* |

### L. Tell and describe (person, place, experience)

**Default points.**
- **Speaking** (1 + 1.5 min): the six-point talk plan where it fits (Day 71), past tense for events, and the full time used.
- **Writing:** the points named in the prompt, plus an opening and a closing.

| # | Type | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | S | *Berätta om din bästa vän.* |
| L2 | S | *Berätta om en dag som du aldrig glömmer.* |

| L4 | S | *Berätta om ditt jobb eller dina studier.* |

| L8 | S | *Beskriv vägen från ditt hem till närmaste affär.* |

title: Templates T17-T20
summary: Extra answer templates for gaps in the practice book.

sections.title: Overview
sections.markdown:
*This file goes with `YKI-EXAM-FIRST-PLAN.md` (section 2.3, templates T1–T16) and `YKI-EXAM-FIRST-CURRICULUM.md`. It adds four slot templates for the tasks in the practice book that no template T1–T16 covers, and it proposes where to teach them.*

**Source of the gap.** The learner's practice book, *Förbered dig för allmän språkexamen* (Gimara Oy), was catalogued task by task: 232 entries (225 tasks + 7 warm-up sections). **49 tasks fit no template T1–T16 well** [Book count]. Book tasks are named here only by their catalogue id, and the id starts with the book page: `p112-R2` is Reagera item 2 on page 112. No sentence from the book is copied. All examples are new situations.

**Since 16 November 2026, T17–T20 belong to the reference library.** The learner memorises only the core (plan section 1); the lines in this file are looked up when a task needs them. The T-numbers stay as aliases, so the book map still works.

**Second review (16 November 2026).** Each full example now has a **short version** next to it: learn the short one first, and add the expanded one later. **Answer length** (third review): practise at about 80 words a minute, so a 20-second turn holds about 25–33 words, a 25-second turn about 33–40, 1 minute about 80 and 1.5 minutes about 120. Short models fit these numbers; they are practice aims, not exam rules. **T20 is optional library material**, not a compulsory early block (T17 stays, because 18 book tasks need it). Success is marked **Green, Amber or Red** (plan section 1): Green, move on; Amber, move on and put the top 1–2 mistakes on the error list; Red, repeat the skill tomorrow with new details. Times and counts below are targets, never gates.

**All Swedish in this file is AI-written and has not been checked by a teacher or a native speaker.** The "required points" are this plan's own reading of each task type. No official checklist exists for these tasks [Plan's own].

Square brackets [ ] are slots, as in section 2.3. G1–G10 are the grammar points in section 2.9 of the plan.

| Template | Gap it closes | Weak-fit book tasks covered | Taught on |
|---|---|---|---|
| T17 | Polite objection: ask someone to stop, or stand up for yourself | 18 | Day 22 (part 1) and Day 24 (part 2): extra 15-minute blocks |
| T18 | Describe a habit, routine, hobby, place or thing | 21 | Day 34b (part 1) and Day 38b (part 2): full study days since the third review |
| T19 | Compare your home country with Finland | 4 (and helps 6 more) | Day 31: an extra 15-minute block, cut to 2 core frames in the third review |
| T20 | One-offs: resign, give things away, say you are afraid, appeal a decision, persuade a stranger | 6 | **Optional** library block, not part of Day 30 |

The covered lists add up to exactly the 49 weak-fit tasks, each once. The day each task is used (a day number, the question bank, optional for the six T20 tasks, or held back) is in `data/assignments.json` and in the book map. Since 16 November 2026 the book map's Template column carries these tags (T17a, T17b, T18a, T18b, T19, T20a–e); three rows put another tag first (`p52-B4`: T18a, then T19; `p123-BA`: T13, then T19; `p62-R6`: T2, then T18b).

sections.title: 1. The templates
sections.markdown:
### T17. Polite objection: ask someone to stop, or stand up for yourself

**When to use:**
- Someone near you does something that bothers you or is unfair: noise, music, a phone call, pushing in, sitting in your seat, treating an animal or a child badly.
- A friend or colleague has let you down, and you want to say so calmly.
- Someone doubts you or complains about you, and you must stand up for yourself (your turn, your seat, your age, what really happened).
- It is face to face, or a phone call about your own behaviour. A shop, a firm or a bill uses T4 or T5 instead.

**The formula:** notice → ask → reason → thank (or say the next step).

**Step 1: notice.** Get attention softly, then name what you see.
- *Ursäkta, …* (Excuse me, …)
- *Förlåt att jag stör, men …* (Sorry to disturb you, but …)
- To a friend: *Du, [Sara], kan vi prata en sekund?* (Hey, Sara, can we talk for a second?)
- *Jag ser att [du pratar i telefon].* (I can see that you are talking on the phone.)
- *Jag tror att [du sitter på min plats].* (I think you are sitting in my seat.)

**Step 2: ask.** Say exactly what you want.
- *Skulle du kunna [prata lite tystare]?* (Could you talk a bit more quietly?)
- *Kan du vara snäll och [sänka musiken]?* (Could you please turn the music down?)
- When it is serious: *Det är inte okej att [lämna hunden i en varm bil].* (It is not OK to leave the dog in a hot car.)
- *Snälla, sluta [___].* (Please stop ___.)

**Step 3: reason.**
- *…, eftersom [jag försöker läsa].* (…, because I'm trying to read.)
- *Jag mår inte så bra, och [musiken är ganska hög].* (I don't feel very well, and the music is quite loud.)
- *Det kan vara farligt för [barnen].* (It can be dangerous for the children.)

**Step 4: thank, or say the next step.**
- *Tack!* (Thanks!) The short, safe close: it fits every T17 situation, and it is the one to use when you are unsure.
- *Tack för att du förstår.* (Thanks for understanding.) Polite but firm: it assumes the person will agree, so use it to end a firm request (a repeated or serious problem), before the person has answered. With a friend, or after a soft request, *Tack!* sounds warmer.
- *Tack, det var snällt av dig.* (Thanks, that's kind of you. Only after the person has agreed or helped.)
- If the person says no: *Då måste jag tyvärr prata med [personalen].* (Then I'm afraid I have to talk to the staff.)

**Part 2 lines: stand up for yourself, or talk to someone you know.**
- Your turn: *Ursäkta, men jag var här före [honom].* (Excuse me, but I was here before him.)
- Your seat: *Jag har en platsbiljett: vagn [fyra], plats [tolv].* (I have a seat reservation: car 4, seat 12.)
- Your age: *Jag förstår att du måste kontrollera, men jag är [tjugofem] år. Här är mitt id-kort.* (I understand that you have to check, but I am 25. Here is my ID card.)
- Someone complains about you: *Jag förstår att [ni är irriterade], men det stämmer inte riktigt.* (I understand that you are annoyed, but that's not quite right.) *Vi [stängde av musiken klockan elva].* (We turned the music off at eleven.) *Jag ber om ursäkt för [ljudet], och det händer inte igen.* (I apologise for the noise, and it won't happen again.)
- A friend or colleague: *Jag blev ledsen när [du pratade om mig med andra].* (I was hurt when you talked about me with other people.) *Vi bestämde att [___], men [___].* (We agreed that ___, but ___.) *Nästa gång vill jag att du [säger till först].* (Next time I want you to tell me first.) *Kan vi prata om det?* (Can we talk about it?)

**Full example** (Reagera, 20 s prep + 25 s [Teacher, unofficial]). Situation: you booked the laundry room in your building, and a neighbour has taken your wet washing out of the machine.

**Short (learn this first, 18 words):** *Ursäkta! Jag har bokat tvättstugan till klockan nio. Kan du vänta lite? Jag behöver tvätta i dag. Tack!*

(Excuse me! I've booked the laundry room until nine. Can you wait a bit? I need to do my washing today. Thanks!)

**Expanded (add later):** *Ursäkta! Jag ser att du har tagit ut min tvätt ur maskinen. Jag har bokat tvättstugan till klockan nio i kväll. Skulle du kunna vänta tills min tid är slut? Jag måste tvätta i dag, eftersom jag reser i morgon. Tack för att du förstår!*

(Excuse me! I can see that you've taken my washing out of the machine. I've booked the laundry room until nine tonight. Could you wait until my time is over? I have to do my washing today, because I'm travelling tomorrow. Thanks for understanding!)

The expanded version has 45 words: at the practice pace of about 80 words a minute that is about 34 seconds, too long for a 25-second turn. In a 25-second Reagera, say the short version plus one sentence (about 30 words); keep the expanded version for a longer turn or a written note. It ends with the firm close (*Tack för att du förstår!*); the short one ends with the safe *Tack!*.

**Common errors:**
- *Ursäkta, kan du att prata tystare?* → *Ursäkta, kan du prata lite tystare?* (G4: no *att* after a modal verb)
- *…, eftersom jag mår inte bra.* → *…, eftersom jag inte mår bra.* (G2: after *eftersom*, *inte* goes before the verb)

**Required points a rater would look for** [Plan's own]:
- **Stranger (part 1):** a polite opener; what the problem is; a clear request; a reason; a thank-you or a next step.
- **Standing up for yourself (part 2):** a polite opener; the fact (I was first, my seat, my age, what really happened); proof if you have it (a ticket, an ID card); a calm request; a close.
- **Friend or colleague:** what happened; how you feel; what you want next time; a way forward (*Kan vi prata om det?*).
- **Tone:** firm but polite. A bare *Sluta!*, or an insult, does not answer the task. Aim for about 25 seconds (a target, not a gate).

**Book tasks it covers (18):**
- Part 1, a stranger (Day 22 block): p34-R3 (boys teasing a classmate), p51-R10 (noisy children at the next table), p51-R12 (dog left in a hot car), p62-R4 (dumping an appliance in nature), p62-R8 (mistreating an animal), p72-R4 (a driver nearly hits you), p112-R2 (loud phone call in a library), p112-R11 (loud music on the bus), p112-R13 (noisy eater at the cinema), p113-R15 (a stranger's child and an unsuitable programme).
- Part 2, stand up for yourself or talk to someone you know (Day 24 block): p112-R3 (served after a later customer), p112-R4 (a doorman doubts your age), p112-R9 (someone in your reserved seat), p34-R14 (a friend spoke badly about you), p51-R2 (a friend returned your car with an empty tank), p87-R9 (a colleague broke an agreement), p112-R10 (a friend stays on their phone), p32-D11 (you are the one complained about: a 7-turn call).
- **Forced fits, said honestly:**
  - p32-D11 is a whole phone call in which you defend yourself. Use the T1 phone frame plus the part 2 "someone complains about you" lines.
  - p113-R15 is a child, so use only the gentle lines (*Förlåt att jag stör …*, a simple reason) and no *Det är inte okej*.
  - p34-R3, p51-R12 and p62-R8 are about someone else's safety. Add an offer: *Ska jag ringa efter hjälp?* (Shall I call for help?)
- **Also helps** (catalogued under another template): p54-S2 (written: ask someone to stop sending gifts, T8) and p62-R2 (ask a relative to stop feeding ducks, T11).

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

---

### T18. Describe a habit, routine, hobby, place or thing

**When to use:**
- A Berätta topic (1 min prep + 1.5 min [Official sample timing]) or a Reagera item about **how you live**: your normal day, your habits, a hobby, how you get around, how you look after your health. This is part 1.
- A topic about **what something is like**: your home, your area, nature, a summer cottage, a book or film, your own style. This is part 2.
- T14 is for a person and T15 is for one past event. T18 is for what you **usually** do, and for what a place or thing **is like**.

**Part 1: habits, routines and hobbies** (Day 34b)
- Open: *Jag vill berätta om [min vardag / mina vanor / min hobby].* (I want to tell you about my everyday life / my habits / my hobby.)
- How often:
  - *Jag brukar [gå upp klockan sju].* (I usually get up at seven.)
  - *Varje dag [cyklar jag till jobbet].* (Every day I cycle to work.)
  - *Ibland [jobbar jag hemma].* (Sometimes I work at home.)
  - *En gång i veckan [spelar jag badminton].* (Once a week I play badminton.)
  - *Jag [tränar] nästan aldrig.* (I almost never exercise.)
- Weekly habits use the plural day: *på lördagar* means every Saturday, while *på lördag* means this Saturday (G9).
- Order: *Först [äter jag frukost]. Sedan [tar jag bussen]. Efter jobbet [handlar jag].* (First I have breakfast. Then I take the bus. After work I do the shopping.)
- Hobby:
  - *Jag har [spelat schack] i [fem] år.* (I have played chess for five years.)
  - *Det kostar [inte så mycket]. Man behöver bara [ett bräde].* (It doesn't cost much. You only need a board.)
- Feeling:
  - *Det bästa är att [jag träffar mina vänner].* (The best thing is that I meet my friends.)
  - *Jag tycker inte om [att stressa på morgonen].* (I don't like rushing in the morning.)
- Then and now: *Förr [åt jag mycket godis], men nu [äter jag mer frukt].* (I used to eat a lot of sweets, but now I eat more fruit.)

**Part 2: a place or a thing** (Day 38b)
- Open: *Jag vill berätta om [vår stuga / mitt kvarter / en bok som är viktig för mig].* (I want to tell you about our cottage / my neighbourhood / a book that matters to me.)
- Where:
  - *Den ligger [i Sibbo], ungefär [en timme] från [Helsingfors].* (It is in Sibbo, about an hour from Helsinki.)
  - *Det ligger nära [havet], bredvid [en liten skog].* (It is near the sea, next to a small forest.)
- What it is like:
  - *Den är [liten och gammal], men [mysig].* (It is small and old, but cosy.)
  - *Det finns [en bastu och en brygga].* (There is a sauna and a jetty.)
- What you do there:
  - *Där brukar vi [bada och grilla].* (There we usually swim and have a barbecue.)
  - *På vintern kan man [åka skidor].* (In winter you can ski.)
- Why it matters: *Den är viktig för mig eftersom [jag kan vila där].* (It is important to me because I can rest there.)
- For a message or a neighbourhood: *En fördel är att [det är lugnt]. En nackdel är att [bussen går sällan].* (One advantage is that it is quiet. One disadvantage is that the bus runs rarely.)
- Close (both parts): *Det var lite om [min hobby].* (That was a little about my hobby.) / *Därför tycker jag mycket om [___].* (That is why I really like ___.)

**Full example** (Berätta, 1 min prep + 1.5 min). Topic: a place you go to often.

**Short (learn this first, 48 words):** *Jag vill berätta om simhallen nära mitt hem i Esbo. Den är ny och ljus. Det finns två bassänger och en bastu. Jag brukar simma där två gånger i veckan. Först simmar jag, sedan går jag i bastun. Den är viktig för mig eftersom jag kan vila där.*

(I want to tell you about the swimming hall near my home in Espoo. It is new and bright. There are two pools and a sauna. I usually swim there twice a week. First I swim, then I go to the sauna. It is important to me because I can rest there.)

**Expanded (add later):** *Jag vill berätta om simhallen i Hagalund, nära min lägenhet i Esbo. Den ligger bara tio minuter från mitt hem, bredvid en stor park. Simhallen är ganska ny och ljus, och det finns två bassänger och en bastu. Jag brukar simma där två gånger i veckan, på tisdagar och torsdagar. Först simmar jag en halvtimme. Sedan går jag i bastun och vilar lite. Ibland tar jag med min dotter, och då leker vi i den lilla bassängen. Det kostar inte så mycket, ungefär sex euro. Förr tränade jag nästan aldrig, men nu mår jag mycket bättre. Simhallen är viktig för mig eftersom jag kan glömma jobbet där. En nackdel är att det är mycket folk på lördagar. Det var lite om mitt favoritställe.*

(I want to tell you about the swimming hall in Tapiola, near my flat in Espoo. It is only ten minutes from my home, next to a big park. The swimming hall is quite new and bright, and there are two pools and a sauna. I usually swim there twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. First I swim for half an hour. Then I go to the sauna and rest a little. Sometimes I take my daughter, and then we play in the small pool. It doesn't cost much, about six euros. I used to exercise almost never, but now I feel much better. The swimming hall is important to me because I can forget work there. One disadvantage is that it is very crowded on Saturdays. That was a little about my favourite place.)

The expanded version has about 120 words. That fills 1.5 minutes at a beginner's pace and mixes both parts: a place plus a habit. The short one is about half; add one detail at a time until the talk fills the time.

**Common errors:**
- *Varje dag jag cyklar till jobbet.* → *Varje dag cyklar jag till jobbet.* (G1: after a time or frequency word, the verb comes next)
- *Jag brukar att simma två gånger i veckan.* → *Jag brukar simma två gånger i veckan.* (G4: no *att* after *brukar*)

**Required points a rater would look for** [Plan's own]:
- **Part 1, habits:** what you talk about; "how often" words (aim for two); the order of a normal day or visit (*först, sedan*); one feeling or reason; one change (then and now) or one advantage or disadvantage; a close.
- **Part 2, place or thing:** what it is and where it is; two details of what it is like; what you do there (*brukar*); why it matters (*eftersom*); one advantage or disadvantage; a close.
- **In a message** (p64-S2): a greeting, where you live, two details, one advantage, one disadvantage, a tip or an offer, and a closing.
- **Timing (a target, not a gate):** aim to keep the Berätta talk going for the full 1.5 minutes without repeating yourself. Plan one point for each 15 seconds.

**Book tasks it covers (21):**
- Part 1, habits, routines and hobbies (Day 34b, a full study day): p35-BB (your arguing habits), p52-B1 (you and time), p52-B2 (what kind of arguer you are), p52-B3 (your normal weekday), p53-B5 (how you get around), p73-BB (looking after your body), p73-BD (looking after your brain), p73-BE (staying healthy), p88-BD (a normal working day), p114-BF (how you spend money when you travel), p114-BI (your hobby), p106-D6 (a phone survey about your internet habits).
- Part 2, a place or a thing (Day 38b, a full study day): p12-D1 (a friend visits your flat: describe the home), p35-BC (your clothes and style), p62-R6 (what matters to you in a neighbourhood), p62-R7 (describe Finnish nature to a friend abroad), p62-BA (nature and your home surroundings), p63-BC (a landscape that matters to you), p64-S2 (a written message: describe your area to a friend who may move), p113-BA (a book or film that matters to you), p114-BE (summer cottages).
- **Forced fits, said honestly:**
  - p106-D6 is a phone survey. Use T1 to open and close, and the "how often" lines to answer.
  - p35-BC mixes T16 appearance lines with T18 habits, and its last question is an opinion (T13).
  - p62-R6 is preferences, so add *Det är viktigt för mig att [det finns en park nära].* (It is important to me that there is a park nearby.)
  - p73-BD ends with tips, so borrow T11: *Det är en bra idé att …*
  - p73-BE asks about your last illness at the end: one T15 sentence in the past.

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

### T19. Compare your home country with Finland

**When to use:**
- Berätta, Din åsikt or Skriva tasks that ask how something is "in your home country" and "here": school, food, healthcare, taxes, parties, clothes, art, daily life, identity.
- In Din åsikt, give your answer to the statement first (T13 step 1). Then use T19 for the reasons.

**The frame:** your link to both countries → the home-country side → the Finland side → one thing that is the same → your view → close.

- Your link:
  - *Jag kommer från [Indien], men jag har bott i Finland i [fyra] år.* (I come from India, but I have lived in Finland for four years.)
  - *Jag vill jämföra [skolan] i mitt hemland och i Finland.* (I want to compare schools in my home country and in Finland.)
- Home-country side: *I mitt hemland [börjar barnen skolan när de är sex].* (In my home country children start school when they are six.)
- Finland side: *…, men i Finland [börjar de när de är sju].* (…, but in Finland they start when they are seven.)
- The rule for both halves: the place comes first, so the verb comes next (G1). *men* does not count as the first part (G10), so *i Finland* is first in the second half and the verb follows it.
- The same: *I båda länderna [är familjen viktig].* (In both countries the family is important.) / *Det är likadant i Finland.* (It is the same in Finland.)
- The biggest difference: *Den största skillnaden är att [skolmaten är gratis här].* (The biggest difference is that school meals are free here.)
- Comparing: *[Maten] är [billigare] i [Indien] än i Finland.* (Food is cheaper in India than in Finland.) The comparative ends in *-are* (taught in full on Day 52).
- Your view:
  - *Jag tycker att [det finska systemet] är bättre, eftersom [___].* (I think the Finnish system is better, because ___.)
  - *Jag saknar [maten] från mitt hemland.* (I miss the food from my home country.)
  - *Det bästa med Finland är att [___].* (The best thing about Finland is that ___.)
- Identity: *Jag känner mig hemma både i [Indien] och i Finland.* (I feel at home both in India and in Finland.)
- Close: *Båda länderna har alltså fördelar och nackdelar.* (So both countries have advantages and disadvantages.) / *Därför tycker jag att [___].* (That is why I think ___.)

**Full example** (Berätta, 1 min prep + 1.5 min). Topic: public transport in your home country and in Finland.

**Short (learn this first, 50 words):** *Jag kommer från Indien, men jag har bott i Finland i fyra år. I Indien åker många människor motorcykel, men i Finland åker man ofta buss eller tåg. I båda länderna är det ganska billigt att åka buss. Jag tycker att kollektivtrafiken är bättre i Finland, eftersom den är tryggare.*

(I come from India, but I have lived in Finland for four years. In India many people go by motorbike, but in Finland people often go by bus or train. In both countries it is quite cheap to take the bus. I think public transport is better in Finland, because it is safer.)

**Expanded (add later):** *Jag kommer från Pune i Indien, men jag har bott i Esbo i fyra år. Jag vill jämföra kollektivtrafiken i mitt hemland och i Finland. I mitt hemland åker många människor buss eller motorcykel, men i Finland åker man ofta buss, tåg eller metro. I Pune är bussarna ofta fulla, och de kommer inte alltid i tid. Här i Esbo går bussarna nästan alltid enligt tidtabellen. Den största skillnaden är att man kan köpa biljetten i en app här. I båda länderna är det ganska billigt att åka buss. En nackdel i Finland är att man måste vänta ute i kylan på vintern. Ändå tycker jag att kollektivtrafiken är bättre i Finland, eftersom den är tryggare och punktligare. Men jag saknar att åka motorcykel med min bror!*

(I come from Pune in India, but I have lived in Espoo for four years. I want to compare public transport in my home country and in Finland. In my home country many people go by bus or motorbike, but in Finland people often go by bus, train or metro. In Pune the buses are often full, and they don't always come on time. Here in Espoo the buses almost always run on schedule. The biggest difference is that you can buy the ticket in an app here. In both countries it is quite cheap to take the bus. One disadvantage in Finland is that you have to wait outside in the cold in winter. Still, I think public transport is better in Finland, because it is safer and more punctual. But I miss riding a motorbike with my brother!)

The expanded version has about 125 words.

**Common errors:**
- *…, men i Finland man åker ofta tåg.* → *…, men i Finland åker man ofta tåg.* (G1: in the second half, *i Finland* is first, so the verb comes next)
- *Maten är mer billig i Indien.* → *Maten är billigare i Indien än i Finland.* (comparative with *-are … än*)

**Required points a rater would look for** [Plan's own]:
- Both countries are named.
- At least two concrete differences, each with an example.
- At least one thing that is the same.
- Your own view with a reason.
- A close.
- In Din åsikt, an answer to the statement in the first sentence.
- In a Skriva opinion text, at least three reasons, as in the official sample [Official sample].

**Book tasks it covers (4):** p88-BA (your home country's school system and Finland's), p52-B4 (restaurants: how often you go, home country versus Finland), p123-BA (your origins and what citizenship means to you), p115-OD (Finnish art compared with art where you grew up).
- **Forced fits, said honestly:**
  - p123-BA is about identity, so it needs the *Jag känner mig hemma både i … och i …* line and T13 reasons more than facts.
  - p52-B4 starts as a habit talk, so use the T18 part 1 "how often" lines first.
- **Also helps** (statements catalogued under T13): p53-O3 (is daily life in Finland easy?), p74-OC (healthcare here), p89-OF (raising children in the Nordic countries), p124-OD (tax levels), p37-OI (how well Finns dress) and p36-OA (are parties here boring?).

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

### T20. One-offs: five small moves (optional library material)

**Optional since 16 November 2026 (second review).** These situations are rare: 6 of 225 book tasks. Look a move up when a task needs it; you do not have to learn T20 early. The block is not part of Day 30 (its optional slots are given with the block in the last section).

**When to use:** each move fits one kind of task that comes up only once or twice in the practice book. These moves fall outside the top five functions, like T16. Each is short: 3–6 lines. **Use only the move the task asks for.**

**T20a. Resigning politely** (to your boss, face to face)
- *Har du tid en minut? Jag har en sak att berätta.* (Do you have a minute? I have something to tell you.)
- *Jag har fått ett nytt jobb, så jag vill säga upp mig.* (I have got a new job, so I want to resign.) An easier alternative: *så jag vill sluta här*. (so I want to leave.)
- *Min sista arbetsdag blir [den 31 maj].* (My last working day will be 31 May.)
- *Tack för [de här åren]. Jag har lärt mig mycket här.* (Thank you for these years. I have learned a lot here.)
- *Jag kan hjälpa till att lära upp [en ny person].* (I can help train a new person.)

**T20b. Offering things for free**
- *Jag ska flytta i [maj], och jag har saker som jag inte behöver.* (I'm moving in May, and I have things that I don't need.) Inside the *som*-clause, *inte* goes before the verb (G2).
- *Vill du ha [min soffa]? Du får den gratis.* (Do you want my sofa? You can have it for free.)
- *Den är [fem år gammal], men den är i bra skick.* (It is five years old, but it is in good condition. These are the T3 seller lines.)
- *Du måste bara hämta den själv före [den 20 maj].* (You just have to collect it yourself before 20 May.)
- *Säg till om du vill ha något!* (Tell me if you want anything!)

**T20c. Saying you are afraid or worried, and asking for what you need**
- *Förlåt, jag är lite nervös. Jag är rädd för [sprutor].* (Sorry, I'm a bit nervous. I'm afraid of needles.)
- *Kan du berätta vad du ska göra innan du börjar?* (Can you tell me what you are going to do before you start?)
- *Får jag ligga ner? Jag blev yr förra gången.* (May I lie down? I felt dizzy last time.)
- *Tack, det känns bättre nu.* (Thanks, that feels better now.)
- With no listener (bad news about yourself): *Oj nej! [Fem kilo] mer än i [januari]! Nu måste jag börja [röra på mig mer].* (Oh no! Five kilos more than in January! Now I have to start moving more.)

**T20d. A written appeal against an official decision**
- *Bästa mottagare,* (Dear recipient,)
- *Jag skriver angående ert beslut [den 3 mars] om [___].* (I am writing about your decision of 3 March about ___.)
- *Jag tycker att beslutet är fel, av tre skäl.* (I think the decision is wrong, for three reasons.)
- *För det första [___]. För det andra [___]. För det tredje [___].* (First … Second … Third …; the verb comes next, G1)
- *Därför ber jag er att [ändra beslutet].* (Therefore I ask you to change the decision.)
- *Jag skickar [mitt intyg] som bilaga.* (I am sending my certificate as an attachment.)
- *Ni når mig på [telefonnummer] eller [e-postadress].* *Med vänliga hälsningar, [för- och efternamn]* (You can reach me on … or … Kind regards, …)

**T20e. Persuading a stranger to give something up**
- *Ursäkta, får jag fråga en sak?* (Excuse me, may I ask something?)
- *Jag ser att du har [den sista stolen] av den här modellen.* (I can see that you have the last chair of this model.)
- *Jag behöver den verkligen, eftersom [jag redan har tre likadana hemma].* (I really need it, because I already have three identical ones at home.) After *eftersom*, *redan* goes before the verb (G2).
- *Skulle du kunna tänka dig att [ta en annan]?* (Would you consider taking another one?)
- *Jag kan [hjälpa dig att hitta en annan].* (I can help you find another one.)
- If the answer is no: *Okej, jag förstår. Tack ändå!* (OK, I understand. Thanks anyway!)

**Full example** (T20d, Skriva, formal, about 20 minutes [Plan's own]). Situation: the city gave your daughter a day-care place far from home.

**Short (learn this first, 60 words):** *Bästa mottagare, Jag skriver angående ert beslut den 3 mars om en dagvårdsplats för min dotter. Jag tycker att beslutet är fel. För det första tar resan nästan en timme. För det andra har vi ingen bil. Därför ber jag er att ge henne en plats nära Hagalund. Ni når mig på 040 123 4567. Med vänliga hälsningar, Alex Kumar*

(Dear recipient, I am writing about your decision of 3 March on a day-care place for my daughter. I think the decision is wrong. First, the journey takes almost an hour. Second, we have no car. Therefore I ask you to give her a place near Tapiola. You can reach me on 040 123 4567. Kind regards, Alex Kumar)

**Expanded (add later):**

*Bästa mottagare,*

*Jag skriver angående ert beslut den 3 mars om dagvårdsplats för min dotter Asha Kumar, född 2023. Hon fick en plats på daghemmet Solrosen i Köklax, men vi bor i Hagalund. Jag tycker att beslutet är fel, av tre skäl. För det första tar resan med buss nästan en timme åt varje håll. För det andra har vi ingen bil, så vi kan inte köra henne dit. För det tredje börjar jag på ett nytt jobb i augusti, och jag måste vara på jobbet klockan åtta. Därför ber jag er att ge Asha en plats på ett daghem i Hagalund eller nära Hagalund. Jag skickar mitt arbetsavtal som bilaga. Ni når mig på 040 123 4567 eller alex.kumar@exempel.fi.*

*Med vänliga hälsningar,*
*Alex Kumar*

(Dear recipient, I am writing about your decision of 3 March on a day-care place for my daughter Asha Kumar, born 2023. She got a place at Solrosen day-care centre in Kauklahti, but we live in Tapiola. I think the decision is wrong, for three reasons. First, the bus journey takes almost an hour each way. Second, we have no car, so we cannot drive her there. Third, I start a new job in August, and I have to be at work at eight. Therefore I ask you to give Asha a place at a day-care centre in or near Tapiola. I am sending my employment contract as an attachment. You can reach me on 040 123 4567 or alex.kumar@exempel.fi. Kind regards, Alex Kumar)

The expanded version has about 120 words. The name, the e-mail address and the phone number are invented.

**Common errors:**
- *Därför jag ber er att ändra beslutet.* → *Därför ber jag er att ändra beslutet.* (G1: *därför* needs the verb next, G10)
- *Jag är rädd av sprutor.* → *Jag är rädd för sprutor.* (*rädd för*: learn it as one chunk)

**Required points a rater would look for** [Plan's own]:
- **T20a, resign:** a polite opener; the decision; the reason; the last day; a thank-you; an offer to help with the handover.
- **T20b, give away:** what you give; that it is free; its condition; when and how to collect it; a friendly close.
- **T20c, afraid:** the feeling; what you are afraid of; what you need (a question); a thank-you. With no listener: the reaction, the fact, and what you will do now.
- **T20d, appeal:** which decision (its date and subject); that you disagree; two or three reasons; what you want them to do; an attachment if you have proof; contact details; a formal opening and closing. These are the official complaint sample's points, adapted from a bill to a decision [Official sample, adapted].
- **T20e, persuade:** a polite opener; what you want; a reason; a question; an offer or a compromise; a polite answer to a no.

**Book tasks it covers (6):** p87-R6 (T20a: tell your boss you are leaving for a new job), p62-R5 (T20b: moving house, offer things to a friend), p72-R5 (T20c: afraid of needles at a blood test), p72-R12 (T20c: bad news on the bathroom scales), p125-S2 (T20d: written appeal against a refused course place), p51-R7 (T20e: persuade a customer to give up the last chair).
- **Forced fit, said honestly:** p72-R12 has no listener. It is a reaction to your own news, so only the last T20c line fits, plus one T18 "then and now" sentence.

**[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]**

sections.title: 2. Where they are taught, and why not only on Days 36–40
sections.markdown:
**The count that decides it.** The rule for weak-fit tasks is to use each one on the day its new template is taught, or on the next two study days.
- If all four blocks sat on Days 36–40, those windows could reach only Day 40, because Days 41–42 are the Phase 2 exit test. That is 5 study days, or about 75 minutes of book time at 15 minutes a day.
- The 49 weak-fit tasks need about 150 minutes, because 20 of them are 2.5-minute talks (19 Berätta and one Din åsikt). The estimate is this plan's own: 2 minutes per Reagera, 3 per talk, 5 per dialogue and 15 per written text, done once and ticked against the points.
- So the blocks are spread over Phase 2, each on a day whose new content is light or whose skill the template builds on. Since 16 November 2026 each block replaces the day's own speaking block (minutes 18–33), so the day stays at 60 minutes (load rule 6 in plan section 1); on a 90-minute day, do both.
- **Third review (16 November 2026): only three blocks are left.** Days 22, 24 and 31 keep their extra 15-minute blocks (T17 part 1, T17 part 2, and T19 cut to 2 core frames). T18 is no longer a block: Day 34 was split into 34a (what happened) and 34b (habits, T18 part 1), and Day 38 into 38a (directions and appearance) and 38b (a place or a thing, T18 part 2). Days 34b and 38b are full study days whose speaking task is the block's book tasks. In `data/assignments.json` and the book map their tasks keep the day numbers 34 and 38.
- **Since 16 November 2026 a day holds at most 2 book tasks** (the block days and Days 34b and 38b are a documented exception). So 16 of the 49 weak-fit tasks moved to the question bank in the book map. Since the second review the six T20 tasks (with p125-S2) are optional and on no fixed day. The table shows the new placement.
- A "study day" here skips light, rest, mock and exit-test days. For example, the window of Day 34b is Days 34b, 36 and 37, because Day 35 is a light day.

| Block | Day | Why this day | Book tasks in the window (day: ids) |
|---|---|---|---|
| T17 part 1: a stranger | 22 | Day 22 teaches the core reactions from 16–30, *Ursäkta* and Reagera timing. T4 (*Problemet är att …*, Day 18) and *eftersom* (Day 8) are known. | 22: p34-R3, p51-R10, p51-R12, p62-R4, p62-R8 · 24: p112-R13, p113-R15 · bank: p72-R4, p112-R2, p112-R11 |
| T17 part 2: stand up for yourself | 24 | Day 24 revisits T8 (first taught on Day 8), so its new content is light. A polite "no" and a polite "please stop" sit well together. | 24: p112-R3, p112-R4, p112-R9 · 25: p32-D11, p34-R14 · bank: p51-R2, p87-R9, p112-R10 |
| T20 one-offs (**optional**, not part of Day 30) | after 30 | Day 30 drills the core reason pairs. Persuading and appealing both run on reasons. T9 (Day 23), T3 (Day 16) and T5 (Day 19) are known. | optional slots only: p87-R6, p62-R5, p72-R5, p51-R7, p72-R12, and the written p125-S2 |
| T19 compare | 31 | Day 31 teaches the other view (*Å andra sidan*). A comparison is two sides by nature. | 31: p115-OD, p53-O3, p36-OG · 33: p88-BA · bank: p52-B4, p123-BA |
| T18 part 1: habits | 34b | Day 34a teaches *först / sedan / till slut* for the past. T18 uses the same words in the present tense, on its own study day. | 34b: p52-B3, p35-BB, p52-B1 · 36: p53-B5, p106-D6 · 37: p88-BD, p114-BI · bank: p52-B2, p73-BB, p73-BD, p73-BE, p114-BF |
| T18 part 2: a place or a thing | 38b | Day 38a teaches place words (*bredvid, mittemot*) and appearance, the base of "where it is and what it is like"; Day 38b uses them on its own study day. | 38b: p12-D1, p62-R6, p62-R7 · 39: p64-S2 · 40: p62-BA, p113-BA · bank: p35-BC, p63-BC, p114-BE |

**What this changes elsewhere** (first written as suggestions; updated on 16 November 2026, when the plan and curriculum were edited):
- **Day 27, Mock 1 preparation:** T17 is taught by then but is not tested in Mock 1. Leave it out of the Day 27 warm-up, as the curriculum already does for T11 and T13–T16.
- **Days 27, 55 and 82, the pre-mock days:** the template recital is gone. In its place come five random prompts, each from a different engine (plan 3.3).
- **Days 34–40:** these days now hold only T18 book tasks. So the first book tasks for T15, T11, T12 and T16 come later, on Phase 3 topic days and in the Phase 4 sets.
- **Phase 3 exit test (4.4):** it asks for 2 prompts from "the less common functions (T11, T12 or T16)". T17–T19 could join that list; T20 is optional and stays out.
- **T20 optional (second review, 16 November 2026):** the T20 block is not part of Day 30. Day 30 keeps its own speaking block. The block, its five book tasks and `p125-S2` are used only in an optional slot: a 90-minute day after Day 42, a rotation or fix day in the cycle after Day 84, or a day when one of its book tasks comes up.
- **Section 5 calendar, "Chunks / banks" column:** add "+ T17 part 1" (Day 22), "+ T17 part 2" (Day 24), "+ T20" (Day 30; since the second review "optional T20 block", not part of the day), "+ T19" (Day 31), "+ T18 part 1" (Day 34) and "+ T18 part 2" (Day 38). Done on 16 November 2026. Since the third review the two T18 parts sit on Days 34b and 38b as full study days.
